postings.title: Career Mentor & Job Placement Specialist
postings.descriptionText:
Our vision: Mastering machine learning is hard, frustrating, and takes time. The talent shortage is the mother of all problems in AI. At Anyone AI, we upskill people from LatAm to solve the AI talent gap through an accelerated and practical training program dictated by AI industry experts. In AI, people are the new capital, and we invest in them in exchange for a share of their future income.



Our mission: Anyone AI's mission is to discover and empower AI talent in Latin America, to build the largest hub and community of AI developers in the region. Our goal is to bridge the talent gap by supplying thousands of skilled developers from Latin America to global markets, particularly the United States, thereby addressing the shortage of AI talent.



We are founding members of Deep Vision AI, one of the first companies in the computer vision / AI space, which was acquired in early 2020 by DFW Capital Partners. Anyone AI is backed by top global investors like GFC (Global Founders Capital) -investors in Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack, Canva, Trivago, Delivery Hero, Revolut, etc-, Canvas Ventures (early investor in Coursera, Evernote, MuleSoft, etc) and Latitud Fund (the largest community of angel investors for LatAm).



Run the race of your life

This is a chance to help change the AI industry and change thousands of people’s lives in LatAm. This position provides self-motivated, collaborative individuals the opportunity to make a direct impact on Anyone AI products and services. You will have the opportunity to challenge yourself while contributing to developing a revolutionary accelerated training program designed to invest in people from LatAm and help them master ML and AI to land a job in less than 6 months.



About the Role

In this hands-on senior role, you will lead the process of sourcing semi-senior and senior candidates, plus the interview preparation process in our training programs to place Anyone AI Fellows in the US and LATAM markets.



Responsibilities



 - Lead and manage the Job Preparation Program for the ML Fellowship, providing guidance to Fellows on: (a) building LinkedIn profiles that attract recruiter interest and increase visibility, crafting résumés that pass HR filters and impress hiring managers, and writing compelling cover letters; and (b) overseeing interview preparation, conducting mock interviews, and advising on negotiation strategies, among other tasks.

 - Conduct onboarding sessions to understand Fellows’ career objectives and expectations.

 - Provide personalized 1:1 sessions and weekly check-ins with job seekers until they secure a new role in AI.

 - Manage the job-seeking and preparation tools provided by Anyone AI or third-party software providers.

 - Collaborate closely with companies to introduce Fellows to hiring managers in the US and LATAM.

 - Report on key metrics, including the number of Fellows actively seeking jobs, job applications submitted, interviews conducted, offers received, cohort placement rates, and average salaries, using a designated tool by Anyone AI.

 - Collect and analyze feedback to propose improvements to the training program and job preparation process.

 - Serve as the main point of contact and provide ongoing support to Fellows post-placement (after they have secured employment).



Skills & Experience

 - Bachelor, Master, or related study in human resources, communication, or technology.

 - Previous experience in qualifying candidates, interviewing and assessing potential hires for technology positions, ideally data science, ML Engineering or AI-related positions in the US and/or LATAM.

 - Previous experience developing and executing job preparation strategies and programs.

 - Highly analytical and data-driven individual, able to work independently and make decisions in real-time.

 - Experience working with a diverse multicultural team. Thrive in a quick, dynamic environment with an iterative development process.

 - Strong entrepreneurial and growth mindset.

 - Excellent team player that builds trust internally and with our Fellows, customers, and partners.

 - Strong work ethic and a "get-the-job-done" attitude in a fast-paced, startup environment.

 - Ability to work collaboratively across many functions and with different teams within the organization.

 - Highly effective and professional communication skills with a track record of communicating complex processes to entry-level or junior team members and helping them thrive in their work environments.

 - Working proficiency in English and Spanish languages.




Anyone AI is an equal opportunity employer. We do not make hiring, employment, or promotion decisions based on race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender or identity or expression, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, marital status, height and/or weight.

postings.descriptionText:
- Location: Remote

 - Type: Contract / Part-time

 - Commitment: 20 hours per week

 - Compensation: Up to 40 USD / hr

 - Project duration: 2 months, with potential extension




ABOUT THE ROLE

We create high-quality STEM training data for frontier AI models used by leading AI labs to improve model reasoning in scientific domains.

We are seeking experts in Biology to create challenging, deterministic problems with exactly one verifiable correct answer. Problems should reflect authentic scientific and analytical workflows and be submitted with complete, verified solutions.

Depending on specialization, work may include molecular biology, genetics, systems biology, computational biology, bioinformatics, or adjacent quantitative biology fields.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design advanced biology problems that challenge frontier AI systems

 - Create deterministic tasks with one correct answer

 - Submit complete, verified solutions

 - Build problems involving experimental reasoning, biological systems, computational analysis, or bioinformatics workflows

 - Use Python and, when relevant, specialized biology or bioinformatics tools

 - Ensure high standards of rigor, reproducibility, and technical clarity




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Master’s or PhD in Biology or a related life sciences field

 - Research or industry experience involving computational or quantitative biological analysis

 - Strong Python skills; experience with data analysis or bioinformatics workflows preferred

 - Strong reasoning ability and comfort with multi-step scientific problem solving

 - Ability to create original, difficult problems grounded in real biological practice

 - Clear written English and strong attention to detail
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with bioinformatics toolkits, genomics workflows, structural biology tools, or computational biology methods

 - Experience designing technical assessments or scientific challenge problems

 - Cross-disciplinary experience spanning biology and computation

postings.descriptionText:
Help shape the future of AI by evaluating how conversational AI agents communicate and perform across different languages.

 - Location: Remote / Global, subject to project location restrictions

 - Type: Independent contractor / Project-based

 - Commitment: To be confirmed

 - Compensation: To be confirmed

 - Project duration: 2–3 months
   
   


ABOUT THE ROLE

At Anyone AI, we create high-quality training and evaluation data for frontier AI models.

We’re looking for multilingual audio evaluators with strong spoken-language proficiency and technical literacy to assess conversational AI agents.

In this role, you’ll participate in live, real-time roleplay scenarios, capture session recordings and technical logs, label conversation transcripts, and evaluate interactions using structured rubrics. Your feedback will help improve the quality and reliability of AI conversations across languages.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Prepare and confirm the required tools and access before each live session.

 - Conduct live, real-time roleplay scenarios with conversational AI agents.

 - Capture recordings, session IDs, and tool-call or console logs.

 - Label conversation transcripts according to project guidelines.

 - Score interactions against structured evaluation rubrics.

 - Provide clear written explanations supporting your scores.

 - Read, validate, and troubleshoot JSON, identifying structural and formatting issues.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - C1/C2 spoken fluency in at least one of the target languages listed below.

 - Ability to demonstrate language proficiency through a speaking and listening assessment.

 - Strong JSON skills, including reading, validation, troubleshooting, and identifying structural or formatting errors.

 - Comfort using digital tools and collecting recordings and technical logs.

 - Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow evaluation guidelines consistently.

 - Clear written communication and sound judgment when assessing AI interactions.


LANGUAGES WE’RE HIRING FOR

 - Welsh

 - Dutch

 - Greek

 - Italian

 - French

 - German

 - Portuguese


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in AI evaluation, audio annotation, or transcript labeling.

 - A background in technical support, quality assurance, or software development.

 - Familiarity with conversational AI, APIs, and structured data.

Responsabilidades:

 - Optimizar la conversión del ecommerce (CRO): fichas de producto, landings y checkout.

 - Ejecutar y analizar A/B testing sobre elementos clave (CTAs, layouts, copy).

 - Monitorear métricas de performance y detectar desvíos (conversión, CAC, revenue).

 - Liderar la estrategia de SEO on-page y crecimiento de tráfico orgánico.

 - Gestionar Google Analytics 4 y construir insights accionables.

 - Analizar performance de campañas (Meta Ads, Google Ads) y recomendar mejoras.¿

 - Implementar estrategias de growth (cross-sell, suscripciones, referidos).

 - Colaborar con equipos de contenido, data y marketing para mejorar resultados.

 - 



Requisitos:

 - 2–4 años de experiencia en marketing digital con foco en ecommerce D2C.

 - Experiencia en plataformas como Tienda Nube y/o Shopify.

 - Manejo avanzado de Google Analytics 4.

 - Experiencia en CRO (conversion optimization) y análisis de funnels.

 - Conocimientos sólidos de SEO on-page y técnico.

 - Experiencia analizando campañas de paid media (Meta / Google).



Se valorará:

 - Pensamiento analítico y orientación a resultados.

 - Proactividad y autonomía.

 - Capacidad de transformar datos en decisiones.

postings.title: Head of Payments
postings.descriptionText:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As our Head of Payments, you will own payment performance end-to-end, with a strong focus on authorization rates, recurring payments, transaction routing, chargebacks, compliance, and payment costs.

This is a highly hands-on role with a significant focus on the US payments ecosystem. You’ll work directly with payment data, PSPs, acquirers, and internal teams to identify opportunities, solve performance issues, and drive measurable improvements across the payment lifecycle.

At Acentecom, we believe that a strong payments ecosystem is essential to creating seamless customer experiences and enabling sustainable growth. We’re looking for someone who understands the details behind payment performance and can turn that expertise into measurable business impact.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Own and continuously improve front-end authorization rates, identifying decline patterns and opportunities to increase successful initial transactions.

 - Own and continuously improve recurring and subscription authorization rates, optimizing retries, dunning, timing, and recovery strategies to maximize successful rebills.

 - Own transaction routing and cascading, continuously optimizing how transactions are routed across the payments ecosystem to improve approval performance and resilience.

 - Own chargeback performance and card-network monitoring, including VAMP and other Visa and Mastercard requirements, ensuring risk metrics remain within healthy thresholds.

 - Drive payment cost optimization, understanding the economics behind processing and working directly with PSPs and acquirers to optimize pricing, fees, and commercial terms.

 - Use payment data to diagnose issues and identify opportunities, translating decline codes, authorization trends, dispute data, and provider performance into concrete actions.

 - Partner directly with PSPs, acquirers, card networks, and internal teams to resolve payment issues and continuously improve performance.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Strong hands-on payments experience within high-volume e-commerce, subscription, DTC, or a similarly complex consumer business.

 - Deep experience with the US payments ecosystem, including payment processing, acquiring, authorization behavior, card networks, and recurring payments.

 - Proven ownership of initial and recurring authorization rates, with experience identifying and implementing changes that materially improve payment performance.

 - Strong hands-on experience with MIDs, PSPs, acquirers, transaction routing, cascading, retries, and dunning optimization.

 - Deep understanding of chargebacks, disputes, fraud, and card-network monitoring programs, including VAMP and Visa/Mastercard thresholds.

 - Strong commercial understanding of payments, including processing costs, pricing models, provider fees, and PSP/acquirer negotiations.

 - Strong analytical skills and the ability to work directly with payment data, dashboards, decline codes, approval trends, and dispute metrics to identify problems and drive solutions.

 - A highly proactive, ownership-driven approach. You’re comfortable getting into the details, solving problems directly, and taking accountability for payment performance rather than operating only at a strategic level.

 - Strong communication and cross-functional skills, with the ability to work effectively with Engineering, Finance, Customer Support, and external payment partners.

postings.title: Treasury Analyst
postings.descriptionText:
As our Treasury Analyst, you will own the day-to-day visibility and accuracy of our cash position across a multi-brand, multi-entity DTC e-commerce business. You’ll make sure we know where our cash is, how it’s moving, and what we expect it to look like ahead, giving the team reliable data to make better financial decisions.

This is a highly hands-on role for someone who is comfortable working across banks, payment processors, legal entities, and currencies. You’ll manage cash reporting and forecasting, processor and bank reconciliations, intercompany activity, payment runs, and working capital while helping us build more scalable and reliable treasury processes.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN

 - Maintain an accurate daily consolidated cash position across all legal entities and banking partners.

 - Build and maintain a rolling 13-week cash forecast, identifying and explaining key changes, risks, and variances week over week.

 - Reconcile payment processor settlements to bank deposits and the general ledger, including settlement timing, reserves, and deposit mechanics.

 - Track and document intercompany transfers across entities, keeping balances, schedules, and supporting documentation accurate and current.

 - Prepare payment runs by gathering approved invoices, scheduling payments, and maintaining clear supporting documentation for approval.

 - Maintain working capital reporting across supplier payment terms, deposits, balance schedules, and cash conversion cycles, updating cash models as terms change.

 - Monitor chargebacks and disputes and maintain clear visibility into their impact on cash.

 - Track merchant account health, including reserve levels, processing limits, and decline patterns, identifying and escalating anomalies early.

 - Maintain accurate bank account records across entities, including signatories, access, and mandates.

 - Support month-end close through accurate and timely cash and bank reconciliations.

 - Help standardize cash forecasting, settlement reconciliation, and treasury processes as we continue building a more scalable financial infrastructure.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience in treasury, cash management, financial operations, payments reconciliation, or a related role.

 - Strong experience reconciling high-volume transaction data across payment processors, marketplaces, banks, or similar environments.

 - Experience building and maintaining cash forecasts, ideally including rolling short-term cash forecasting.

 - Strong understanding of payment processor settlements, including timing differences, reserves, deposits, and reconciliation.

 - Experience working across multiple legal entities and currencies.

 - Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, with the ability to build and maintain reliable financial models rather than simply work from existing templates.

 - Experience with accounting platforms such as QuickBooks Online and payment processors such as Adyen, Stripe, or similar tools.

 - Familiarity with subscription and rebill businesses and the impact of chargebacks, disputes, reserves, and processing performance on cash.

 - Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the persistence to investigate discrepancies across multiple systems until they reconcile.

 - A highly proactive and autonomous approach. You’re comfortable identifying issues early, investigating root causes, and driving them through resolution without requiring detailed direction.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to maintain accurate documentation and clearly explain cash movements, variances, and risks.

 - Fluent English.

postings.title: Content Localization Specialist (Korean / Chinese - Simplified)
postings.descriptionText:
ABOUT US

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.




ABOUT THIS ROLE

We are looking for a talented multilingual superstar (Korean/Simplified Chinese/English) with skills and backgrounds in translation and localization. The primary contribution is to localize our in-app content for the Korean market. The secondary contribution is to create high-quality Simplified Chinese content for the Korean market with training and support.
We want an expert with excellent oral and written communication skills in both languages. This candidate should have a sharp linguistic understanding of both Simplified Chinese and Korean, with working professional proficiency in English.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Content translation and localization
   
   - Perform Korean-Simplified Chinese translation and localization for in-app learning and marketing content from a pedagogical perspective.
   
   - Iterate and polish the translated/localized content based on QA tasks in pursuit of an optimal learning experience to Koreans learners teaching Chinese

 - Content development and writing
   
   - If needed, design and write in-app learning materials (e.g., lesson scripts, activities, vocabulary lists) in a systematic way for Korean learners at different levels of Simplified Chinese proficiency under training and guidance of the manager.

 - Content project support
   
   - If needed, support operation of content-related projects, such as uploading scripts, QAing lessons, coordinate pieces of the operation under training and guidance of the manager.

 - Communication and collaboration with international team members
   
   - Receive directions well form the manager, implement instructions, complete projects, and maintain clear communication from end-to-end.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR




REQUIRED

 - Native Simplified Chinese and native or near-native English writing and speaking skills

 - Deep understanding of both languages and the status quo of Simplified Chinese learning in Korea

 - Demonstrated experience and expertise in Korean-Simplified Chinese translation and localization

 - Experience in Simplified Chinese teaching, language pedagogy, or curriculum design

 - Great attention to detail with a strong sense of ownership and agency

 - Passion for technology-assisted language learning and willingness to learn and use advanced technologies for work

 - Working proficiency in English

 - A fast learner, team player, skilled communicator, and creative problem-solver




PREFERRED

 - Experience working in educational technology (EdTech)

 - Experience using AI tools (e.g., LLMs, generators, internal tools) to create instructionally sound, pedagogically aligned, and scalable learning materials




WHAT WE’RE EXPECTING

While we respect contractors’ flexibility and ownership of their own schedule, we expect the localizer / writer to work for 15 – 20 hours a week on average. It is highly likely that more than 20 hours a week is appreciated, depending on the workload and the availability. We completely understand that availability may fluctuate and we also respect contractors’ request to take time off. But we also expect a somewhat regular work schedule or hours in most occasions. All in all, maintaining clear communication with the manager is certainly expected.




WHY WORK AT SPEAK

 1. Join a fantastic, tight-knit team at the right time: we're growing very quickly, we've most recently raised our Series C from some of the top investors in the valley, and we've achieved product-market fit in our initial markets. You'd join at a magical time when a single person could significantly change the course of the company.

 2. Do your life's work with people you’ll love working with: we care strongly about our craft and want every person at Speak to feel like they're growing every day. We believe in the idea that working with people you both enjoy and have respect for makes everything better. We hire thoughtfully and only work with people we admire deeply.

 3. Global in nature: We're live in over 40 countries and launching in a number of new markets soon. We have dedicated offices in San Francisco, Ljubljana, Seoul, Tokyo, and Taipei, and you’ll have the opportunity to talk to users in each of these regions on a regular basis as well as travel.

 4. Impact people's lives in a major way: Learning a language is one of the single most life-changing skills one can learn, and right now 99% of people never achieve their goal because the process is broken. We’re helping millions of people achieve their goals and improve their lives.

Speak does not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build so it doesn't happen twice. For every fix, ship the runbook or tool that stops it recurring

 - Close the loop to Product. Surface patterns, not one-offs, backed by metrics

 - Raise the team's floor. Lift what the whole team can resolve, not just what you can

 - Know where your scope ends. Escalate genuine product bugs and outages with a clean reproduction, not a shrug

 - Within 90 days, name the top recurring failure patterns and attack them at the root, not just patch symptoms


WHO YOU ARE

The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.

 - You solve problems end to end. Given a customer, some logs, and a vague symptom, you find the break and can tell a customer-side cause from a product bug

 - You're fluent with AI agents and prompts. You've built or debugged LLM workflows and know how they break: prompts, knowledge bases, retrieval, the gap between test and live

 - You're excited to build automation, not just fix what's in front of you. You think in leverage. This is the signal that matters most

Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.

 - You like talking to customers. You'll get on a call and resolve the real problem live, not just the reported one

 - Comfortable in our core stack (Node.js, TypeScript, React, Express) or close enough to ramp fast

 - Fluent with AI coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) to script, clean data, or navigate a new codebase fast

 - You own problems nobody assigned you, and you make the people around you better through docs and walkthroughs

Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.

 - Observability tooling (Grafana, Honeycomb, Sentry)

 - Internal tooling that turned manual work into a system

 - Ecommerce or DTC exposure

Not a Fit If:

 - You stop at "it's not our bug" instead of finding the real cause

 - You'd rather build the fix than talk to the customer who hit it

 - You want a backlog of well-scoped tickets, not ambiguous production fires


WHY SIENA?

Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.

Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.

A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.

A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.

Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.

Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.

AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.


OUR VALUES

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.


OUR APPROACH TO AI

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.


HOW WE HIRE

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at talent@siena.cx.

postings.title: Especialista de Producto - Argentina
postings.descriptionText:
Sobre Halter:

En Halter, nuestra misión es ayudar a los productores y ganaderos a gestionar sus operaciones de forma más productiva y sustentable. Nuestros clientes usan Halter para liberarse de las limitaciones de las prácticas convencionales. ¿Te imaginás ver a 500 animales levantarse y caminar tranquilamente hacia su próxima parcela? Sin cuatriciclos, sin perros, sin alambrados. Solo un rodeo caminando a su ritmo. La gente dice que parece magia. Nuestros clientes están revolucionando el pastoreo con Halter. Está cambiando vidas y transformando toda una industria. 

La gente se suma a Halter para hacer un trabajo con propósito. Al unirte a nosotros, vas a estar resolviendo problemas desafiantes dentro de un equipo de primer nivel y una cultura pensada para el alto rendimiento. Nuestro equipo piensa distinto, trabaja más duro y se compromete más. Estamos comprometidos a generar un cambio real en el mundo — no es fácil, y la verdad es que nos encanta que sea así de difícil. 

Contamos con el respaldo de inversores de primer nivel como Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Peter Beck de Rocket Lab e Icehouse Ventures. 

Para saber más, visitá nuestro LinkedIn e Instagram. 

Estamos buscando un Especialista de Producto que actúe como el principal representante de Halter en América del Sur durante nuestro lanzamiento en la región. Este es un rol pionero. Vas a trabajar directamente con nuestros primeros productores mientras desplegamos Halter en sus campos, aprendiendo qué hace falta para que el producto funcione de manera brillante en este entorno, y transmitiendo esos aprendizajes al resto de la empresa para que podamos construir e iterar en consecuencia. 

Vas a trabajar de cerca con la casa central de Halter en Nueva Zelanda y con nuestros equipos comerciales en América del Sur para asegurarte de que el producto entregue valor innegable desde el primer día y que estemos construyendo lo correcto para nuestros productores. 

Halter es una de las AgTech de más rápido crecimiento del mundo, y la tecnología más transformadora disponible para el pastoreo a base de pasturas. Con los collares y la app de Halter, los productores pueden cercar y mover virtualmente su ganado, y monitorear en tiempo real la ubicación y el comportamiento del mismo. 

Buscamos personas con visión amplia que entiendan cómo hacer que las cosas sucedan — gente que resuelve problemas de forma natural y se siente cómoda en un entorno dinámico y de alta energía donde va a ser desafiada a diario. Nuestra persona ideal es alguien profundamente comprometido con entender nuestro producto y las necesidades de nuestros clientes. Sobre todo, te va a importar el ganado y los productores que trabajan con él, y vas a defender sus intereses en toda la

organización. 

Se requiere disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional e internacional en este rol. 

 

Sobre el rol:

¿Cómo podría ser tu día a día? 

• Salir a los campos para ayudar a desplegar Halter con nuestros primeros clientes — esto es trabajo de campo, no de escritorio. 

• Construir relaciones sólidas con nuestros productores pioneros, entender en profundidad cómo operan y aprender qué necesita hacer el producto para entregar valor real en este contexto. 

• Transmitir esos aprendizajes de forma clara y rigurosa a nuestros equipos de producto e ingeniería en Nueva Zelanda, para que siempre estemos construyendo lo que más importa. 

• Ayudarnos a entender los matices de la producción ganadera en América del Sur — los animales, la tierra, las prácticas — y compartir ese contexto en toda la empresa. 

• Pensar de forma crítica sobre el producto de principio a fin e identificar qué necesitamos corregir, mejorar o construir a continuación. 

• Trabajar con nuestros primeros clientes para asegurarte de que estén aprovechando al máximo Halter y viendo resultados reales. 

• Colaborar con el equipo comercial para mantener una fuerte alineación a medida que escalamos. 

• Hacer todo lo necesario para que Halter triunfe en Sudamérica. 


Lo que buscamos: 

• Experiencia trabajando en la producción ganadera de América del Sur. Esto es requisito excluyente. 

• Pasión por los animales y el futuro de la ganadería en la región. 

• Interés por la tecnología y genuina curiosidad por cómo funciona nuestro producto. 

• Un comunicador sólido que pueda traducir lo que ve en el campo en feedback claro y accionable para un equipo remoto de producto e ingeniería. 

• Capacidad demostrada para pensar de forma crítica ante un problema y llegar a conclusiones sólidas e innovadoras. 

• Comodidad con la incertidumbre. Esta es una entrada temprana al mercado y las cosas van a ser imperfectas; vas a prosperar con eso en lugar de frustrarte. 

• Aprendizaje rápido con las ganas de trabajar duro junto a un equipo que está haciendo cosas que nunca se hicieron antes. 

• Una actitud de "manos a la obra" con la resiliencia para superar los desafíos. 

• Disponibilidad para viajar y trabajar de forma flexible, incluyendo fines de semana cuando sea necesario.

• Se requiere dominio del idioma inglés para colaborar con la casa central.

El dominio del inglés es un requisito para esta posición. El proceso de selección incluirá entrevistas en inglés y una parte significativa del trabajo diario también se desarrollará en este idioma. Buscamos personas que se sientan cómodas comunicándose, participando en conversaciones profesionales y trabajando efectivamente en inglés. Si no te sentís cómodo/a manteniendo conversaciones profesionales en inglés, esta posición probablemente no sea adecuada para vos.



Sumate al equipo:

Halter está comprometida con promover un lugar de trabajo diverso e inclusivo — un espacio donde cada uno pueda ser uno mismo y hacer el mejor trabajo de su vida. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:


 - 3-5 years of experience in relationship management/account management roles.

 - Experience in dairy farming or within the agriculture sector with a deep passion for helping farmers succeed.

 - Strong business acumen.

 - Positive attitude and collaborative team player who excels at overcoming challenges.

 - The ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced working environment with a high degree of autonomy.

 - A hunger for success and personal growth, and an eagerness to evolve alongside a world-class team.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE:


 - Revenue Retention & Expansion: You will own the retention, renewals and expansion targets of Halter’s existing revenue in the region.

 - Ensure farmers are extracting full value from Halter to achieve their goals and ultimately understand the impact it’s having on their farming business.

 - Account Management: Responsible for renewing customer agreements and expanding the revenue of existing Halter customers, by adding value in every interaction to drive on-farm goals and performance.

 - Deployment: Supporting the onboarding, training and implementation of the Halter system on customers' farms, ensuring all relevant farm owners, managers, and workers are able to successfully use the system.

 - Relationship Building: Proactively cultivate genuine and trustworthy relationships with farmers, their teams, and families, fostering strong connections and understanding.

 - Farmer Success: Strategically partnering with customers to establish clear business goals, timelines, priorities and metrics of success.

 - Problem-Solving: Provide prompt and effective communication and support to farmers and team members, addressing technical or operational challenges with expertise and efficiency.

 - Community & Networking: Represent the Halter brand with pride, lead local discussion groups, and proactively build strong networks within the community for increased brand visibility and connections.

 - Customer Advocate: Acting as the voice of the customer and bridging the gap with our product teams to provide important context about what is happening on the ground with our farmers and their animals.

 - Technical Expertise: Working closely with our product teams to provide technical and practical advice from a farmer’s perspective on everything reproduction, pasture and agronomy.

 - Contribute to a positive team environment, supporting others to succeed and role modelling Halter’s Operating Principles.




OUR BENEFITS:

 - Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.

 - Healthy body, healthy mind. We're partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.

 - We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

 - Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.







HALTER IN AUSTRALIA:

Halter entered Tasmania two years ago and has rapidly expanded to now have 20% of the state's dairy herd with Halter - a thriving customer base managed by a talented, local team. Halter recently entered Queensland and NSW, and now has a growing team and customer base across both states.

In Victoria and South Australia, Halter is preparing to launch operations following recent regulatory approval for virtual fencing. In Western Australia, Halter does not yet have customers. In these states there is a groundswell of demand for Halter across thousands of farmers. In Australia, virtual fencing is regulated by individual states' animal welfare legislation. Until recently, several states had legislation that did not permit farmers to use high-quality virtual fencing technology. With NSW parliament's announcement regulating virtual fencing, and Victoria and South Australia following suit, these barriers are now lifting.

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. The only way we achieve that is by improving our product based on the root cause of each failure that occurs in the field - those investigations happen in our Failure Analysis lab.

As a Failure Analysis Technician, you'll be the hands at the start of every failure investigation. You'll receive returned collars from the field, put them through incoming inspection and triage, tear down units to preserve the evidence, and run the test setups that replicate failures. You'll close out the failure modes we already understand, and hand the novel failures to our Failure Analysis Engineers as a clean, complete evidence package. You'll also own the logistics of getting samples to external labs.

This is a hands-on, high-volume, detail-driven role. We're looking for someone who wants to be genuinely excellent at the craft of getting evidence out of failed hardware. WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Perform incoming returns inspection and triage

 - Classify units into the correct disposition and close out common documented failure modes.

 - Carry out controlled teardown to the team's defined procedure on standard unit types, preserving evidence for downstream analysis; including recording of findings, photographs, measurements in the team’s Failure Analysis system

 - Build, wire and configure test setups; run tests and capture results

 - Package, document and ship samples to external labs

 - Other duties as required from time to time.

 - Hands-on experience in a lab, workshop, production or field service environment - an electronics, mechatronics or engineering background is preferred

Behind that network is our Network team, and standing between farmers and that team is CX.

We're looking for a Technical Specialist/Software Engineer - Network to join the CX team and take ownership of resolving network and connectivity issues before they reach the Network team, while building the T2 team's ability to root cause and solve more of these issues themselves. You'll be the first line of defence for all incoming tickets related to collar connectivity, reliability, and performance, and will play a key role in resolving issues quickly, escalating effectively, and shielding the Network team from noise so they can focus on the deeper engineering work that needs their expertise.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build internal tooling (dashboards, playbooks, monitors, etc.) to streamline triage workflows and improve visibility into comms-related tickets

 - Investigate on-farm connectivity issues and surface insights to the Network team to improve coverage, performance, and robustness

 - Collaborate closely with the Network and Fleet teams to proactively detect patterns, flag potential issues, and improve first-line resolution

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. We’re looking for a highly capable and first-principled individual to join our Reliability & Failure Analysis team and build quicker, more accurate processes to debug failed hardware to root cause, both from the field and lab testing. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. To achieve this, we need to know about every failure in the field and how to eliminate it.


You’ll be responsible for building a team that debugs and diagnoses failed hardware, including collars and tower components, to deeply understand the root cause. Halter products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices, and debugging and root-causing the many different failure modes that occur requires highly skilled engineers who are inquisitive and methodical. This is both a technical and operational role where you will be central to closing the feedback loop between our lab & field performance and our engineering teams, ensuring that every failure is investigated, understood, and used to improve product reliability. This is a critical role to enable growth across the globe.


Our aspiration is to resource this team to increase accuracy and throughput, while lifting the deep technical competency and lab capabilities onsite in our Auckland office. This is a huge opportunity for the right person - you will have a lasting impact on farmers across the globe.

 - Ownership of the returns pipeline end-to-end: own intake, safe handling, triage, diagnostics, storage and traceability. Set clear targets for turnaround time, throughput and root-cause accuracy.

 - Iterate the diagnostics process to improve accuracy and reduce no-fault-founds.

 - Personally contribute to the highest-impact or deeply ambiguous failure modes. This is a hands-on role; you’ll be very close to the product.

 - Complete ownership of the failure analysis lab capability: build a roadmap to bring capabilities in-house, such as X-Ray/CT, cross-section, SEM etc.

At Halter, we know how much farmers care - for their animals and their pasture. But the tools they rely on haven’t kept up, and we’re on a mission to change that. Halter helps farmers make smarter decisions - fast. We reckon good pasture management is the key to more productive and sustainable farms. More grass. Healthier soil. Happier animals. And more time back for the people doing the work.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for standout Junior/Intermediate Engineers with a deep product instinct: people who care as much about the problem as the solution. You'll take on challenges that genuinely haven't been solved before. We don't mind whether your strengths sit on the frontend, backend, full stack, or on the platform side that gives every other engineer leverage. What matters is that you ship robust, thoughtful work, lift the bar on how we build, and use AI tools well.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS OUR TEAMS SOLVE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, build, and deliver features and systems end to end, from the surfaces farmers touch to the services and infrastructure behind them.

 - Make smart architectural calls, then back them up by writing the code.

 - Work closely with engineering, design, and product to ship high-impact features quickly.

 - Collaborate with other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and context sharing.

 - Contribute to the reliability and performance of our systems, especially when things get tricky. Every team owns its services end-to-end, with an on-call rotation.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.




YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU

 - Have designed and delivered complex systems in production and have the experience (and scars) to show for it.

 - Think like a product engineer: you care about the customer experience, not just clean code.

 - Know how to use AI tools well to lift team output and focus on the harder stuff.

 - Have experience supporting and collaborating with other engineers.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.




DEPENDING ON WHERE YOU SIT ON THE STACK, SOME OF THESE WILL LAND HARDER THAN OTHERS:

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.

 - Backend: building and scaling REST APIs, distributed systems, and event-driven services. Comfort with both relational and non-relational databases. Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or systems that integrate with hardware/IoT a bonus.

 - Full stack: all of the above, end to end, across web, mobile, and the services that power them.

 - Platform: you love building tooling that makes the whole company move faster, including the AI tooling that's reshaping how engineers work. Strong AWS and Terraform at scale, with experience across CI/CD, observability, and on-call tooling.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction.

In this role, you will prioritise daily efforts that optimise growth performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and other regional sales teams, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of farmers. Your contributions will directly support Halter’s mission to support 50% of the world's habitable landmass to be more productive and sustainable.

This role is based in the South Taranaki region and will require regular travel. 




WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR. 

 - Sales & Customer Success Expertise: Value-based sales experience, with a strong history of creating opportunities, closing deals, and building lasting customer relationships. You understand post-sales value building and have experience upselling to grow partnerships.

 - Beef Industry Experience: You know the ropes of beef operations, understanding the unique challenges of the industry. If you don’t, you will be deeply passionate about it, and willing to dive deep into the operations of a farm to learn rapidly.

 - Attitude: You naturally play for the front of the jersey. Make those around you better. Thrive under pressure and own your results. You bring authentic energy and passion to every interaction.

 - Territory Management: Able to use critical thinking to manage a large territory with a balanced focus on sales and customer success, making the appropriate trade-offs.

 - Problem Solving & Collaboration: Resourceful and quick-thinking, you work well with cross-functional teams to address challenges and drive solutions.

 - Willingness to Travel: Frequent travel within your territory to engage with customers and prospects.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE. 

 - Prospecting & Expansion: Sourcing new leads and opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals, industry events, and other channels, as well as responding to inbound queries. You’ll manage the full sales pipeline from lead generation through to close.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: Manage your pipeline and meet high-growth sales targets by screening, qualifying, demonstrating the product, and successfully negotiating contracts with customers.

 - Customer Account Management: After the sale, maintain close relationships with customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: A high level of ownership in your territory working with regional agricultural groups to foster deep relationships across the beef industry.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.




ABOUT THE ROLE.

As Failure Analysis Lead, you will be the person who answers the critical question: why did this fail? When a collar dies in our ongoing reliability stress screening, or a batch shows unexpected yield loss on the production line, you will be the person who opens it up, gathers the data, and finds the truth. You will work hands-on with a small team of dedicated technicians, systematically investigating failure modes, forming and testing hypotheses, and translating findings into concrete recommendations that flow back to our production and hardware design teams.

Every failure contains information, and your job is to extract that information rigorously and turn it into action: changes to processes, components, test coverage, or design. The right person for this role will be deeply curious, methodical, and comfortable working in ambiguity.

You will be embedded at our contract manufacturer in Thailand, whilst working closely with the Halter Production team and connected directly to hardware design engineers in New Zealand. You will be a critical link in the feedback loop that keeps our product reliable and improving.

This role is based on-site at our manufacturing facility in Thailand. Candidates must be able to work in Thailand on a full-time basis. Thai nationals are strongly encouraged to apply. Regular interaction with our engineering team in New Zealand will be required, with occasional travel.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN.

Failure Investigation

 - Own the end-to-end analysis of all hardware failures from reliability testing, production line yield losses, and any other source in the factory.

 - Conduct structured, first-principles investigations: physical teardown, electrical measurement, data analysis, and hypothesis testing.

 - Work to distinguish between random defects, systematic process issues, design weaknesses, and component quality problems.

 - Own the failure analysis backlog: ensure every failure that requires investigation is triaged, tracked, and resolved to a conclusion.

Root Cause Analysis & Documentation

 - Develop clear failure hypotheses and design experiments to validate or disprove them.

 - Document findings with precision in Notion and create structured debug processes to scale up the team of technicians.

 - Maintain a structured failure database that builds institutional knowledge over time.

Feedback to Production & Design

 - Translate failure analysis findings into evidenced recommendations provided to Production Engineering, Design Engineering, Supplier Quality, or the Contract Manufacturer.

 - Raise issues early when failure trends suggest systemic risk, and support the escalation process where needed.

Managing the Technician Team

 - Direct and coordinate a small team of technicians embedded at Calcomp, assigning debug tasks, maintaining quality of data collection, and developing their technical capability.

 - Set clear standards for how failures are handled, measured, and recorded, and maintain those standards consistently.

 - Build a well-organised, well-equipped failure analysis workflow at the factory.

Reliability Monitoring

 - Monitor HASS testing and results to identify trends, outliers, and emerging failure modes.

 - Contribute to ongoing reliability improvement by connecting data from HASS, production yield, and field returns into a coherent picture of product health.




WHO YOU ARE.

Must-haves

 - A degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Mechatronics, or a related field, with hands-on experience in hardware failure analysis or reliability engineering.

 - Strong practical skills in electronics debugging and experience in investigating hardware failures systematically.

 - High proficiency in written and spoken English.

 - Strong documentation discipline.

 - Comfortable working independently and driving your own workload without close supervision.

Strong advantage

 - Familiarity with reliability testing methodologies: HASS, HALT, thermal cycling, or accelerated life testing.

 - Background in fields where product reliability is non-negotiable.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

About the role:

Halter is scaling rapidly across all states of Australia, and we are looking for the new AU Country Director to accelerate that growth, living at the heart of everything we do in Australia.



This is a role for someone who can build the machine and stay close enough to the field to know whether it’s working. You’ll lead Halter’s Australian market, with full ownership for setting the sales and marketing strategy, building the team, and driving the execution required to grow Halter’s impact for pastoral cattle farmers across Australia.



One day, you'll be working with your leadership team to build out go-to-market strategies that will accelerate growth accross Australia. The next, you’ll be in a boardroom with one of Australia’s largest producers, helping shape a deal that changes how they operate. By the end of the week, you might be on farm with a Territory Manager, listening to what’s actually keeping farmers up at night and turning those insights into sharper sales execution and feedback for other leaders across Halter.



This role owns real commercial outcomes. You’ll be responsible for revenue growth, pipeline quality, forecasting, territory performance, leadership standards, and the culture of the AU Revenue team. You’ll work closely with marketing, customer, product, operations, and global sales leadership to make sure Halter’s go-to-market strategy is sharp, scalable, and deeply connected to the realities of Australian farming.



The impact is significant. Over 40% of Australia's landmass is farmed by Beef or Dairy producers, and Halter is significantly lifting the productivity and sustainability of that land. This is one of the most important growth roles in the business, but also for Australia, and the person who lands it will know that.






WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - We’re looking for a rare kind of market leader, someone who has built high-performing teams before, knows what exceptional looks like, and has the scars, standards, and instincts to prove it.

 - You’ll have led revenue teams in a high-growth environment, ideally across SaaS, technology, agriculture, enterprise sales, or another complex, relationship-led industry. You know how to set a high bar, coach people towards it, and build the kind of team culture where talented people are pushed, supported, and genuinely proud of the work they do. You care deeply about people, but you don’t avoid hard conversations. You give direct feedback, raise standards, and help people achieve more than they thought they were capable of.

 - You’ll also be seriously commercially sharp. You know what’s happening inside your team’s pipeline, conversion rates, deal quality, territory coverage, activity levels, and forecast - not because someone sends you a report, but because you’re close enough to the work to know where the real opportunities and risks are. You don’t wait until the end of the quarter to discover a problem. You spot gaps early, act with pace, and bring people with you. You’re data-driven, but never robotic. You understand that the numbers show you where to look, and the people tell you what’s really going on.

 - This role also needs someone who can move between worlds with ease. Polished enough for the boardroom, real enough for the farm gate. Credible with senior executives, but just as comfortable building trust with the people actually running the farm. Agriculture experience would be a genuine advantage, but more important is respect for the industry, curiosity about how farming businesses operate, and the ability to earn trust with people whose livelihoods depend on the decisions they make.

 - Above all, we’re looking for someone with rare ownership, drive, and presence. Someone who wants the responsibility of building something enormous. Someone who can lead leaders, sell complex deals, raise the bar across a country, and still bring energy, pace, and belief to the team around them.



This is not a role for someone waiting for a perfect playbook. It’s for someone who can build one.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE:

 - Build, develop, and performance-manage a team of Sales & Marketing leaders, setting clear expectations, coaching in the field, levelling up leader

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every dollar the team spends on paid and organic ends up in one place: the website. This role builds the thing that converts it.

You own Halter's website - as an engineer. In the short term that means owning and building in Webflow: shipping landing pages, components, and experiments fast. But the bigger prize is the migration. You'll scope and lead Halter's move off Webflow to a custom, headless-CMS-backed site, then own it as a codebase - fast, flexible, and built to scale across New Zealand, Australia, and the US.

You own the conversion rate that turns visits into leads. The channel owners drive traffic; you own what happens when it lands - page experience, lead forms, load speed, and the technical and on-page SEO that keeps the site fast, crawlable, and ranking. And you're the build partner for ABM: when the Search, SEO & ABM owner needs a personalised landing experience for a target account, you build it to brief.

This is the highest-leverage lever on the team: a better-converting, faster-shipping site multiplies the output of every other channel. You report to the Performance Marketing Lead and own the conversion rate and lead-quality numbers.

You'll do it with AI as a core tool. Page builds, component generation, copy, and test analysis - we expect you to use AI to ship faster and sharpen every output. You know what an MCP server is, and you've automated real work with tools like n8n.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We don't care where you've come from - front-end engineering, growth engineering, web dev, or a designer-developer who ships production code. What matters is that you build fast, and that you've moved a conversion rate and can prove it.

You're a front-end engineer. You're fluent in modern front-end - React/Next.js, TypeScript, HTML/CSS - and component-driven build, and you've worked with a headless CMS. You can own a website as a codebase, not just a page builder.

You can run a migration. You've moved a site - or a meaningful chunk of one - from a hosted platform to a custom build, and you know how to do it without tanking SEO, performance, or the pipeline on the way.

You're an experimenter. You form a hypothesis, run a clean test, read the result honestly, and ship the winner. You build knowledge, not opinions.

You care about the whole journey. You don't stop at the form submit - you track results through the funnel and follow up with the wider team to fix problems wherever they surface, even when they're further down the funnel than your page.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

Building and shipping a new landing page - in Webflow today, in your own components tomorrow - and getting it live in hours, not weeks.

Scoping the headless migration: choosing the stack and CMS, mapping the URL and SEO plan, and sequencing the move so nothing breaks.

Designing and shipping an A/B test on a key landing page, then reading the result and rolling out the winner.

Rebuilding a lead form to cut friction and improve quality, then handing a clean lead off to the right downstream flow.

Working with the Paid Social owner to fix a landing page that's dragging down an otherwise strong campaign, and with the Search owner on technical SEO and page speed.

Building a personalised landing experience for a target enterprise account to an ABM brief.




YOU'LL CRUSH THIS ROLE IF YOU

Own the conversion rate. You're accountable for turning traffic into leads, and you treat the site's conversion rate and lead quality as your number.

Build fast and for real. You ship production-quality pages and components - in Webflow now, in a custom headless stack next - and you can own the migration end-to-end.

Test your way to the answer. You run disciplined experiments, kill what doesn't work, and ship what does. You don't operate on opinions - you build knowledge.

Are AI-native. You know what an MCP server is, you've built things with tools like n8n, and AI is already core to how you work.

 - You've owned website conversion or growth engineering in a high-growth SaaS, hardware, or ag-tech business.

 - You've built in Webflow beyond content - whole pages, custom components, and interactions - and know where it stops scaling.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

At Halter, we know how much farmers care - for their animals and their pasture. But the tools they rely on haven’t kept up, and we’re on a mission to change that. Halter helps farmers make smarter decisions - fast. We reckon good pasture management is the key to more productive and sustainable farms. More grass. Healthier soil. Happier animals. And more time back for the people doing the work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for Lead Engineers who perform at the top of the craft. You'll take on the hardest problems, make the calls that matter on the gnarliest design questions, and ship work that the rest of the team learns from. Engineers around you get better because they're working alongside you. We don't mind whether your strengths sit on the frontend, backend, full stack, or on the platform side that gives every other engineer leverage. What matters is that you ship robust, thoughtful work at a level few others can match, and use AI tools well.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS OUR TEAMS SOLVE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Take on the hardest problems and ship the work that proves them out.

 - Make the architectural calls that matter, then back them up by writing the code.

 - Set the standard for thoughtful engineering: clean, observable, easy-to-evolve code and systems.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Help set the pace and quality bar for engineering at Halter.

 - Help evolve our testing strategies, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure patterns.

 - Own the reliability and performance of your domain, especially when things get tricky. Every team owns its services end-to-end, with an on-call rotation.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.
   
    


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU:

 - Have spent years shipping complex systems in production and have the experience (and scars) to show for it.

 - Stay calm under pressure, have a low ego, and can rally a team through tough or complex work.

 - Think like a product engineer: you care about the customer experience, not just clean code.

 - Know how to use AI tools well to lift team output and focus on the harder stuff.

 - Have grown other engineers by working alongside them, not by managing them.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.
   
    


DEPENDING ON WHERE YOU SIT ON THE STACK, SOME OF THESE WILL LAND HARDER THAN OTHERS:

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.
   
   Backend: building and scaling REST APIs, distributed systems, and event-driven services. Comfort with both relational and non-relational databases. Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or systems that integrate with hardware/IoT a bonus.
   
   Full stack: all of the above, end to end, across web, mobile, and the services that power them.
   
   Platform: you love building tooling that makes the whole company move faster, including the AI tooling that's reshaping how engineers work. Strong AWS and Terraform at scale, with experience across CI/CD, observability, and on-call tooling.
   
    


OUR BENEFITS

 - Delicious snacks

At Halter, we know how much farmers care - for their animals and their pasture. But the tools they rely on haven’t kept up, and we’re on a mission to change that. Halter helps farmers make smarter decisions - fast. We reckon good pasture management is the key to more productive and sustainable farms. More grass. Healthier soil. Happier animals. And more time back for the people doing the work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for standout Senior Engineers with a deep product instinct: people who care as much about the problem as the solution. You'll take on challenges that genuinely haven't been solved before. We don't mind whether your strengths sit on the frontend, backend, full stack, or on the platform side that gives every other engineer leverage. What matters is that you ship robust, thoughtful work, lift the bar on how we build, and use AI tools well.

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.

 - Design, build, and deliver features and systems end to end, from the surfaces farmers touch to the services and infrastructure behind them.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.

 - Have experience supporting and mentoring other engineers.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. We’re looking for a highly capable and first-principled individual to join our Failure Analysis team and debug failed hardware to root cause, both from the field and lab testing. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. To achieve this, we need to know about every failure in the field and how to eliminate it.

You’ll be responsible for debugging and diagnosing failed hardware, including collars and tower components, to deeply understand the root cause. Halter products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices, and debugging and root-causing the many different failure modes that occur requires an inquisitive mindset and methodical approach. This is both a technical and operational role where you will be central to closing the feedback loop between our lab & field performance and our engineering teams, ensuring that each failure is investigated, understood, and used to improve product reliability.

 - Personally contribute to the highest-impact or deeply ambiguous failure modes. This is a hands-on role; you’ll be very close to the product.

 - Actively participate in developing the processes and ways of working, to improve accuracy and reduce no-fault-founds.

 - Mentor and guide junior engineers in their work, with a medium to long term view of expanding their technical knowledge and their approach to failure analysis.

 - Work closely with hardware, firmware, production, supplier quality and networking teams to investigate failures and find root cause.

 - Actively support the recruitment process for hiring out a brilliant team, rooted in excellent process discipline, technical capability and a tenacious curiosity to figure things out.

 - Deep electronics engineering experience, with hands-on experience debugging complex hardware.

 - Experience with diagnosing field failures and understanding the relationships between in-field events and product failures

 - Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate technical findings into clear feedback for cross-functional teams.

 - A natural inclination to share knowledge, to educate and mentor

 - A deep curiosity and principled approach to finding root causes with clear evidence.

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page https://www.halterhq.com/careers for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

 - Recruit and develop high-performing talent, helping scale Territory Manager teams as Halter grows rapidly across the U.S.

You’ll collaborate closely with engineering teams in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where decisions happen quickly, and every contribution makes an impact.

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned.
