At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

We're looking for a Product Specialist to be Halter's boots on the ground as we launch Halter in South America. This is a pioneer role. You'll be working directly with our earliest producers as we deploy Halter onto their farms, learning what it takes to make the product work brilliantly in this environment, and feeding those insights back to the rest of the company so we can build and iterate accordingly.

You'll work closely with Halter's HQ in New Zealand and our commercial teams in South America to make sure the product delivers undeniable value from day one  and that we're building the right things for South American producers.

Halter is one of the world's fastest-growing agritech companies, and the most transformative technology available in pasture-based grazing. With Halter's cattle collars and app, producers can virtually fence and shift their cattle, and proactively monitor cattle locations and behaviour.

We're looking for big thinkers who know how to get stuff done — people who are natural problem-solvers and are comfortable in a dynamic, high-energy environment where they'll be challenged daily. Our ideal person is someone deeply committed to understanding our product and our customers' needs. Above all, you'll care about the cattle and the producers who work with them, and you'll champion their interests across Halter.

National and International travel will be required in this role. 



About the role


What your day could look like:

 - Getting out onto farms to help deploy Halter with our first customers — this is hands-on work, not desk work.

 - Building close relationships with our pioneering producers, deeply understanding how they operate, and learning what the product needs to do to deliver real value in this context.

 - Feeding those learnings back clearly and rigorously to our product and engineering teams in New Zealand, so we're always building what matters most.

 - Helping us understand the nuances of South American cattle production. The animals, the land, the practices and sharing that context throughout the company.

 - Thinking critically about the product end-to-end and identifying what we need to fix, improve, or build next.

 - Working with our first customers to make sure they're getting the most out of Halter and seeing real results.

 - Partnering across the commercial team to maintain strong alignment as we scale.

 - Whatever else it takes to make Halter succeed in South America.


What we're looking for:

 - Experience working in South American cattle production. This is a must-have.

 - Passionate about animals and the future of agriculture in the region.

 - Tech-savvy and genuinely curious about how our product works under the hood.

 - A strong communicator who can translate what they're seeing in the field into clear, actionable feedback for a remote product and engineering team.

 - Proven ability to think critically about a problem and reach strong, innovative conclusions

 - Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage market entry and things will be imperfect; you'll thrive on that rather than be frustrated by it.

 - Fast learner with the drive to work hard alongside a team doing things that have never been done before.

 - A get-stuff-done attitude with the resilience to push through challenges.

 - Willing to travel and work flexibly, including weekends when needed.

 - Spanish fluency required. 

 - English proficiency is a requirement for this role. The recruitment process will include interviews conducted in English, and a significant part of the day-to-day work will also be conducted in English. Candidates should feel comfortable communicating, participating in professional conversations, and working effectively in English. If you are not comfortable having professional conversations in English, this role may not be the right fit for you.

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the South East region in Nebraska, ideally in Columbus. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. We’re looking for a highly capable and first-principled individual to join our Failure Analysis team and debug failed hardware to root cause, both from the field and lab testing. Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. To achieve this, we need to know about every failure in the field and how to eliminate it.

You’ll be responsible for debugging and diagnosing failed hardware, including collars and tower components, to deeply understand the root cause. Halter products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices, and debugging and root-causing the many different failure modes that occur requires an inquisitive mindset and methodical approach. This is both a technical and operational role where you will be central to closing the feedback loop between our lab & field performance and our engineering teams, ensuring that each failure is investigated, understood, and used to improve product reliability.

This is a huge opportunity for the right person - you will have a lasting impact on farmers across the globe.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Personally contribute to high-impact failure modes. This is a hands-on role; you’ll be very close to the product.

 - Actively participate in developing the processes and ways of working, to improve accuracy and reduce no-fault-founds.

 - Work closely with hardware, firmware, production, supplier quality and networking teams to investigate failures and find root cause.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Electronics engineering experience, with hands-on experience debugging hardware.

 - Experience with diagnosing field failures and understanding the relationships between in-field events and product failures

 - Excellent communication skills to share your technical findings with others

 - A deep curiosity and first-principles approach to finding root causes with clear evidence.

 - Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action - you’re not afraid to roll up your sleeves and get stuck into wider challenges when required.

 - Low ego, highly collaborative and willing to play for the front of the Jersey.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is searching for a Lead Supply Quality Engineer to take responsibility for ensuring that every component in our supply chain is delivered at quality and on time.  If you are an expert in implementing and managing quality systems to catch issues early, resolve them quickly, and ensure high-quality components are always delivered on-time at our Contract Manufacturers, we want to talk to you! Our Hardware manufacturing is accelerating quickly to satisfy our growing global markets and it is vital that every component that is shipped to our contract manufacturers in Asia is ready for the tough environment it will face on farm, once it is assembled into Halter hardware.



WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Implement statistical process control methods for the manufacturing process of critical parts and work with the suppliers to ensure this is reflected in their process control plan

 - After a failure during production or OQC inspection at a supplier, run a rapid sprint analysis with design engineers to unblock the release of the shipment with risk-mitigative actions and keep production running with effective preventive measures

 - Update and implement quality control documentation to protect against future failures, based on root cause analysis that identified a component issue after, first flagged when a collar went offline on a farm in Australia

 - Audit the compliance with Halter’s quality requirements at a new supplier and work with the supplier to quickly close any non-conformances you found

 - Frequent travel between Auckland HQ (where you will be based) and China

 


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience in quality management for high-volume manufacturing. Production of electromechanical products is preferred

 - Committed to personal development and staying current with relevant industry standards, methods, and trends

 - Proven experience in responding to and resolving quality issues rapidly to minimise production disruption

 - Demonstrated first principles thinking and ability to hone in on the most important issues during audit or reviewing problems

 - Experience in working with suppliers to achieve required outcomes based on context

 - High proficiency (written, verbal and reading) in English and Mandarin (preferred)

 - Relevant quality-related qualifications such as ASQ certification (for example CQE or CQA) are beneficial, as is formal Internal Auditor Certification

 - Willing to travel regularly to China (50%+ of your time)

 - Someone who will thrive in a close team environment and can work well in the self-directed and demanding environment of a rapidly scaling company

Own the injection moulding tools behind Halter's solar-powered cattle collars. You'll qualify tools built by our supplier partners and keep tens of thousands of parts consistent, from first trial to mass production.

 - High-volume production experience, including keeping tools capable long after sign-off

 - Clear, collaborative communication with suppliers and internal teams, including working through disagreements with data

 - Experience working with contract manufacturers in Asia

 - Hands-on experience with secondary operations

 - Mould flow simulation (e.g. Moldflow)

The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a key member of the Talent leadership team, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering Halter’s global recruitment strategy as we scale rapidly across new and existing markets.

Reporting into the Head of Talent, you’ll lead a growing team, providing direction, coaching, and support to ensure we consistently hire exceptional people who raise the bar and align deeply with our mission and values. You’ll balance hands on recruitment delivery with team leadership, strategic planning, and continuous improvement of our recruitment engine.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys operating at a systems and leadership level, thrives in high-growth environments, and wants to have a meaningful influence on how a company scales, through thoughtful strategy, strong teams, and disciplined execution.



WHAT YOUR DAY WILL LOOK LIKE

 - Lead and develop a team of Recruiters across our Customer and Go To Market portfolio across South America, you’ll set clear expectations, coach for performance, and support career growth.

 - Own recruitment delivery across different portfolios and functions, while ensuring the wider team delivers consistently high-quality hiring outcomes.

 - Partner closely with the Head of Talent on recruitment strategy, workforce planning, and capacity modelling to support near and long term growth.

 - Act as a senior partner to hiring leaders, helping them anticipate talent needs, define success profiles, and make strong, data informed hiring decisions.

 - Design and evolve scalable recruitment processes, tools, and ways of working that support increasing volume without sacrificing quality.

 - Upskill and enable hiring managers through structured coaching, training sessions, and real-time feedback to lift interview quality and assessment rigour.

 - Help shape and refine Halter’s Employee Value Proposition, ensuring our external talent story reflects the real employee experience.

 - Embed inclusive hiring practices across the team, supporting diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives in both process and outcomes.

 - Represent Halter externally as a talent ambassador, at events, industry forums, and universities - strengthening our employer brand.

 - Track, analyse, and share key recruitment metrics to continuously improve performance.

 - Support internal mobility and long-term talent planning initiatives as the business matures.

 - As a fast-moving growth company, you’ll also jump into new challenges and projects as they arise - helping shape how we scale.



WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

 - 8+ years of experience in talent acquisition, ideally within high growth or global tech environments.

 - Proven experience leading and developing a team, including setting standards, managing performance, and scaling team capability.

 - Strong track record recruiting across multiple disciplines and regions (experience with software, hardware, or deeply technical roles is highly valued).

 - A strategic business partner who can operate at multiple levels, from executive discussions and planning through to hands-on hiring execution.

 - Demonstrated success delivering high-volume hiring without compromising on quality or candidate experience.

 - Deep expertise in proactive sourcing strategies and global talent markets.

 - Strong data and reporting capability; comfortable using metrics to guide decisions and improve outcomes.

 - High emotional intelligence, excellent communication skills, and a calm, solutions-focused approach in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.

 - A natural owner, someone who takes accountability, builds trust quickly, and genuinely cares about doing recruitment exceptionally well.

This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Missouri Boot Heel region. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you.  - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. ABOUT THE ROLE

As a South American Launch Specialist, you'll be one of the first people on the ground establishing Halter's presence across the region — and you'll own what it means to bring Halter to producers in Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil for the first time.

You'll lead the rollout of Halter on new operations end-to-end: training cattle and operators, solving problems in the field, and supporting producers as they get started. You'll work directly with ganaderos and pecuaristas — on the estancia, on the fazenda, in the campo — building the onboarding experience that every future customer in the region will inherit.

This role is partially field-based. Expect roughly a 70/30 split toward time on the ground, with regular travel across Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil. You'll be with customers where they run their cattle, and the quality of what you build depends on you being there and understanding their operations deeply..

It's practical, hands-on, and highly ownership-driven. Every operation is different, and you'll tailor each deployment to help producers build confidence with Halter. Because we're early here, your read on what's working — and what local producers actually need — feeds straight back into how we build. You'll work closely with our Product team to make sure Halter meets the realities of South American ranching, not a playbook borrowed from somewhere else.

 - Own deployments from sales handoff through a smooth transition to the broader customer team

 - Travel to estancias and fazendas across Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil to deploy Halter in person

 - Work directly with producers to bring Halter into their operation and support day-to-day use

 - Lead training that fits the operation: practical, straightforward, and useful

 - Act as the main point of contact during deployment, giving customers a clear, reliable owner

 - Partner closely with Sales, Support, Product, and Operations to keep deployments coordinated across borders

 - Keep deployments on track by managing timelines, aligning resources, and clearing blockers

 - Solve problems quickly and adapt plans as conditions change — language, terrain, and infrastructure will all vary

 - Spot patterns in the field and feed them directly to Product to shape how Halter works for the region

 - Set customers up with the confidence and foundation needed for long-term success with Halter

 - Whatever else it takes: This is an early-stage market entry. You’ll do what needs doing to make Halter succeed in South America.



WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience working with customers: whether onboarding, supporting, deploying, or managing complex rollouts

 - Genuine comfort with travel and field work

 - Fluency in Spanish and English, Portuguese is a bonus.

 - Confidence operating independently and keeping priorities organized

 - The ability to coordinate moving pieces and keep things progressing without constant oversight

 - A practical, solutions-focused mindset when challenges come up

 - Comfort working cross-functionally: pulling in the right people and keeping everyone aligned

 - Clear, straightforward communication

 - Good judgment and the ability to adapt when plans change

 - A genuine care for the people we serve and the quality of the work

 - Agriculture or cattle ranching experience, especially with extensive grazing systems

English proficiency is a requirement for this role. The recruitment process will include interviews conducted in English, and a significant part of the day-to-day work will also be conducted in English. Candidates should feel comfortable communicating, participating in professional conversations, and working effectively in English. If you are not comfortable having professional conversations in English, this role may not be the right fit for you.

 - Familiarity with the South American beef sector across one or more of Argentina, Uruguay, or Brazil

 - Experience working in ag-tech

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Southern region of Arkansas. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Recruit and develop high-performing talent, helping scale Territory Manager teams as Halter grows rapidly across the U.S.

As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US. 

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction.

Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers. ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Manager, Commercial Strategy, you'll own the future growth path for Halter. You'll set the commercial strategy that accelerates adoption, unlocks new markets, and helps us win before competitors even see us coming — and you'll roll up your sleeves to make it happen.

Reporting to the VP Commercial Strategy, this is a senior leadership role and a deeply hands-on one. You'll be a key partner to the VP and the wider commercial leadership group, helping shape where Halter plays and how we win — and then doing the work to get there. You'll build and lead a small, high-calibre team over time, but you'll lead from the front: in the model, in the field, and in the detail. This is a player-coach role, not a hands-off one.

You'll move fluidly between the strategy and the paddock — one moment framing a market-entry thesis, the next on the ground with farmers and ranchers pressure-testing it in reality, the next going deep with finance on our CAC model.

This is a rare opportunity to shape one of the most transformative companies in agriculture, lead our most important commercial decisions, and leave your fingerprints on the trajectory of the entire company.



What your day could look like

 - Continuously evolve Halter's commercial strategy - where we play, how we win, and where we place our biggest bets across markets, channels, and segments. You set the commercial strategy and the priorities; then lead your team and partners to execute against them.

 - Be the go-to strategic partner to the VP Commercial on Halter's most consequential commercial decisions.

 - Help to mentor a small, high-performing Commercial Strategy team - while staying hands-on in the work yourself.

 - Do the work - build the models, write the narratives, and run the analysis yourself, not just direct others to.

 - Lead the most complex, cross-functional bets across GTM, Product, and Ops - from new-market entry to new channels and partnerships.

 - Own market intelligence and competitive strategy - anticipating shifts, farmer needs, and macro trends to keep Halter several moves ahead.

 - Set the long-term frameworks for how Halter monetises new capabilities and enters new markets, and hold the org accountable to them.

 - Define and stand up Halter's strategic partnership strategy - identifying, structuring, and scaling the partnership models that unlock new distribution, data, and revenue.

 - Build the financial backbone for big decisions: Opportunity sizing, scenario analysis, and the structures that drive crisp decision-making.

 - Turn complex, ambiguous problems into clear narratives and decisions for leaders and frontline teams.

 - Drive adoption end-to-end - ensuring strategies don't just get approved, but get executed, measured, and improved across the business.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - You're a seasoned commercial strategist who builds real-world engines, not just frameworks, playbooks, and pitch decks.

 - You can crack the messiest, highest-stakes problems, build the model that reveals the answer, and then mobilise the organisation to move.

 - You're deeply commercial. You understand the levers - growth, pricing, unit economics, partnerships, market entry - and you know how and when to pull them.

 - You're a doer first. You'd rather build the model and ship the v1 yourself than delegate it - and your team learns by watching you set the standard.

 - You can build and coach a small team as the function grows, while staying a strong individual contributor in your own right.

 - You earn the trust of senior leaders quickly and can influence decisions without needing positional authority - but you're equally happy in the weeds doing the work.

 - Ambiguity doesn't scare you; you run toward it. You think clearly, communicate crisply, and turn complex ideas into simple, actionable stories people rally behind.

 - You've got range and altitude. One day you're framing a multi-year market thesis; the next you're in the spreadsheet or unblocking sales so the strategy actually lands.

 - You're a champion of cross-functional collaboration - across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Product, and Ops - and you make everyone around you sharper.

ABOUT HALTER

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

About Halter

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association
meetups.



This role covers the North East region of Wyoming. Frequent travel is required as a part of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattlemans, Stockmans associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halter.

We're hiring a People & Performance Partner to build the people foundation from zero to one.

You'll partner with local leaders and the global P&P team to stand up the core people infrastructure for a new market — then keep raising the bar as the team scales.

 - Coaching managers through feedback, performance conversations, development, and early employee relations matters

 - Owning onboarding quality so new starters understand the mission, operating model, and cultural bar from day one

 - Running people logistics — systems, documentation, compliance, and employee information

 - Supporting market-entry operations: office setup, field-team logistics, local vendor coordination, fleet and vehicle processes

 - Staying close to the ground and feeding signal back to People, Talent, Commercial, and leadership

 - Cultural fluency in Argentina and/or Uruguay

 - Comfort in fast-moving, high-standards environments

 - Grit, humility, and a bias toward action

 - Like building before things are fully defined

 - Can move between strategic thinking and hands-on execution

 - Give and receive feedback directly — and help build a culture where others do the same

 - Believe people experience and performance are mutually reinforcing, not in tension

 - Are willing to challenge leaders when the standard is slipping

 - Want to help shape the culture of a new market from day one

English proficiency is a requirement for this role. The recruitment process will include interviews conducted in English, and a significant part of the day-to-day work will also be conducted in English. Candidates should feel comfortable communicating, participating in professional conversations, and working effectively in English. The first people systems in a new market shape everything that follows. If we get this right, local hires will understand Halter's mission and standards from day one, managers will lead with clarity, and the team will move fast without creating people, compliance, or culture debt.

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the Alberta region in Canada.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of Canadian ranchers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the North West region of Saskatchewan. Frequent travel is required as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the cust

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're changing the way the world farms — and with that comes a responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. We're looking for an experienced Electronics Engineer to join our Failure Analysis team and debug failed electronics down to root cause, from both the field and lab testing.

Halter collars aren't serviced, aren't repairable, and need to last 6–10 years, anywhere across the globe. Our products are complex, highly integrated electromechanical devices packed with ultra-low power circuitry, RF, solar and battery systems, high-voltage pulse circuits, and dense multi-layer PCBs. To make them last, we need to understand every electronic failure mode in the field and know exactly how to eliminate it.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Personally own the highest-impact and most ambiguous electronic failure modes, driving them to a clear, evidence-based root cause. This is a hands-on role; you'll be very close to the electronics.

 - Debug and diagnose failed electronics at the sub-system and component level: power generation and conversion, ultra-low power circuits, RF and antenna, battery systems, high-voltage pulse circuits, and the MCUs, SoCs, sensors and interfaces around them.

 - Use the full bench of EE diagnostic tools (oscilloscopes, DMM, network analyzers, signal generators, LCR meters, current clamps, HV meters, thermal imaging, microscopy and X-ray where relevant) to isolate faults.

 - Understand the relationships between in-field events and electronic failures, connecting field data and returns to physical failure signatures on the hardware.

 - Develop and improve the processes, tooling and ways of working that increase diagnostic accuracy and reduce no-fault-founds.

 - Work closely with hardware, firmware, production and supplier quality teams to investigate failures and drive corrective action into the design.

 - Mentor and guide more junior engineers, expanding their technical knowledge and their approach to failure analysis.

 - Support recruitment for building out a brilliant team, rooted in strong process discipline, technical capability and a tenacious curiosity to figure things out.

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role at the board and component level. You'll diagnose failed collar and tower electronics, isolate faults to the specific component, net, or design decision responsible, and translate that understanding into clear, evidence-based feedback that improves product reliability. You'll be central to closing the loop between field and lab performance and our hardware, firmware, and production teams.

This is a huge opportunity for the right person - you'll have a lasting impact on farmers across the globe.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Solid electronics engineering experience, with hands-on expertise diagnosing field failures and connecting real-world events to product failure modes for complex, highly integrated hardware at the board and component level.

 - A methodical, first-principled approach to root cause analysis, backed by clear evidence rather than assumption.

 - Strong grounding in electronic circuit fundamentals across analog, digital, power and RF; ideally including ultra-low power IoT designs, batteries, solar, DC-DC conversion, high-voltage generation and insulation, and interfaces such as I2C and SPI.

 - Proficiency with EE diagnostic and test equipment, and comfortable reading schematics and PCB layouts to trace faults.

 - Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate technical findings into clear, actionable feedback for cross-functional teams.

 - A natural inclination to share knowledge, educate and mentor.

 - A strong sense of ownership and a bias for action — you're not afraid to roll up your sleeves and get stuck into wider challenges when required.

 - Low ego, highly collaborative, and willing to play for the Front of the Jersey.

 - A BE degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or a similar relevant qualification.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Northern region of Arizona. Frequent travel is expected as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halte

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.



This role covers the Southern region of Arizona. Frequent travel is expected as apart of this role.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting New Business: You’re driving up driveways, attending local cattle auctions, meeting with your local Livestock, Cattleman's, Stockman's associations, building your new business pipeline through outbound lead generation efforts. You’re fielding inbound leads in a timely manner, prioritizing administrative tasks with your in-field activities.

 - In-Field Sales: You don’t mind getting your hands and boots dirty. Halter is best discussed over a coffee at a kitchen table, in the horse saddle, or on a side-by-side in a pasture. You’re out on the ranch helping potential customers before diving into the value of Halter. You’re dropping off coffee during calving season. You value the magic moments that make all the difference to our customers.

 - Expanding Existing Opportunities: You’re always looking for new opportunities, and that includes expanding your existing customers with Halter. You find value in expanding relationships and finding new ways to increase value over time. Not every rancher will collar all of their cows, so you see this as a unique opportunity to meet your goals.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: High-growth sales targets don’t scare you; you step up to a challenge and like shooting high. You’re an expert pipeline manager and don’t second-guess unqualifying a lead. You’re able to manage today’s deals while keeping next month in your sights.

 - Customer Account Management: Building relationships is more than just making the sale to you. After the sale, you aim to maintain close relationships with your customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: You have a high level of ownership and take pride in what you build. Owning an entire territory means giving treatment to every corner and leaving no stone unturned. You value being the face of your territory, meeting with high-level stakeholders from various local, state, and federal agencies to build lasting relationships with regional agricultural groups.

 - Customer Onboarding: Your high level of ownership doesn’t stop after the sale. You dive in to make sure your customers have the very best onboarding experience possible. You actively own the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation even when you’ve handed off the customer to different teams across Halte

ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Escalations Specialist, you’ll sit within the Customer Experience Technical team and own our customers’ high-stakes support cases, where the problems are rarely simple. You’ll be the bridge between Support, Product, Territory Managers and Account Managers, resolving the issues that need more than a standard ticket to unblock. You’ll use deep product knowledge, technical investigation and practical farm understanding to get to the bottom of what’s actually going on.

Some of this you’ll solve from your desk, and some of it you’ll solve standing in a paddock. When an issue needs eyes on the ground, you’ll get out on farm to see it firsthand rather than relying on secondhand descriptions. That could be a setup problem, a hardware question, or something in the animals’ behaviour that doesn’t add up.

You’ll also drive customer health and churn recovery across the whole customer base. That means not waiting for things to go wrong. You’ll actively track how customers are doing, spot the early signs of an account heading toward trouble, and work across teams on the plan to turn it around. Then you’ll turn what you learn into upskilling for our Customer Experience Support team by building out playbooks and documenting product insight, to minimise the number of tickets being escalated and improving the overall customer experience.





WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Own escalations: Be the go-to person when something’s gone seriously wrong, taking accountability for high-stakes issues and partnering with Territory Managers and Account Managers to drive them through to resolution.

 - Keep customers in the loop: Give farmers clear, honest updates throughout an escalation so they always know where things stand, especially when the pressure is on.

 - Drive health and churn recovery: Track customer health across the full customer base, spot accounts heading towards trouble early, and own the recovery plan.

 - Investigate properly: Lead complex troubleshooting, pull the right data to understand what actually happened, reproduce issues, and validate bug reports before they go to Product or Engineering.

 - Get on-farm when it matters: Do on-farm investigations when remote diagnosis isn’t enough, validating setups, hardware, animal behavior and environmental factors firsthand.

 - Bridge the teams: Represent escalated customer context internally so the right decisions get made, and translate field and technical findings into improvements across product, process and education.

 - Feedback and improve: Surface patterns, whether behavioral, environmental or hardware-related, and contribute to better support processes, tooling, documentation and escalation playbooks.

 - Upskill the team: Train the Customer Experience Support team to recognise and resolve more complex issues themselves, reducing the number of cases that need to be escalated.

 - Measure what matters: Track and report on escalation and customer health metrics, such as open escalations, time to resolution, customers recovered and recurring issues.

 - Be there when it counts: take part in on-call or roster coverage to support incident response, including weather events and farm-wide outages.





THIS COULD BE FOR YOU IF…

You’ve spent at least 3 years in a customer-facing role, ideally in customer success, account management, technical support or something similar, where you owned the relationship and the outcome, not just the ticket. Beyond that, we don’t mind where you’ve come from: agriculture, hospitality, retail or somewhere else entirely. What matters is that you have a deep, genuine care for customers and their animals, real technical curiosity and good judgement.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our wireless network engineering team - the team that keeps one of the world's largest private IoT networks connected. Over a million devices across New Zealand, Australia, the US and Canada, spanning LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device, running on remote infrastructure in some of the hardest terrain there is.

This isn't a pure delivery or pure people role. You'll be in the work: shaping the network architecture, weighing in on spectrum strategy and link budgets, reviewing the automation that runs our tower fleet, and helping your team do the best work of their careers. You'll need to hold the technical bar high while creating the space for others to grow.

We're solving connectivity problems that haven't been solved before - keeping livestock connected hundreds of kilometres from the nearest town, where there's often no coverage at all. It's a role that demands absolute ownership: someone who can take a blurry problem, create clarity, and lead a team to nail it.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS YOUR TEAM SOLVES

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. The wireless network team owns the connectivity layer everything else depends on:

 - Keeping over a million collars connected across LoRa, cellular, and satellite direct-to-device - in valleys, over ridgelines, and far beyond the edge of conventional coverage.

 - Planning coverage with real RF engineering: link budgets, path loss modelling, antenna selection, and spectrum strategy across multiple regulatory regimes.

 - Running a fleet of thousands of remote towers with zero-touch provisioning, configuration automation, and remote diagnostics - a truck roll to a hill-country site is expensive, so software has to do the work.

 - Squeezing every byte: our devices are power and bandwidth constrained, so protocol efficiency and data optimisation directly shape the product.

 - Making network health visible - turning telemetry from millions of radio links into signals engineers and field teams can act on.

Every team here ships systems that have to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab. As an engineering manager at Halter, you're in the work, not above it: coaching engineers, shaping the technical bets, and staying hands-on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead a team of wireless network engineers - supporting their growth, giving great feedback, running performance conversations, and helping them focus on what matters.

 - Own the technical direction and delivery of the network: architecture, reliability, and scalability across collar-to-tower-to-cloud connectivity.

 - Stay close to the technical details - spectrum allocation and compliance, LoRa and cellular behaviour, tower infrastructure, fleet configuration automation, and the software tooling that ties it together - and bring a strong point of view.

 - Own network reliability outcomes: uptime, incident response, and the on-call practices that keep a 24/7 physical network healthy without burning the team out.

 - Drive tower deployment and coverage strategy as we scale into new regions - site selection, RF planning, and delivery of critical infrastructure.

 - Hire and grow the team. Wireless network engineering is a rare skill mix, and you'll be building a world-class bench of it.

 - Work closely with firmware, backend, hardware, and field operations to shape what we build, not just how. You'll be in the room when requirements are fuzzy and you'll help make them clear.

 - Back engineering-led initiatives and look for opportunities to use AI tools to accelerate development or unlock entirely new ways of working.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters and you'll be expected to develop it.

 - Contribute to the broader engineering culture and practices that make Halter a great place to build.


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU

 - Have led engineers directly - performance conversations, mentoring, hiring, the lot.

 - Have strong wireless networking fundamentals - you're credible on spectrum allocation, path loss, link budgets, and antenna behaviour, and can hold a high technical bar with specialists in these areas.

 - Have hands-on experience with LoRa/L

ABOUT THE ROLE




We're looking for an Events Specialist who's great at doing one thing above all else: making things happen. This role is about rolling up your sleeves and delivering events that connect with Australian cattle and dairy farmers in ways that feel real, not corporate.

You'll work across a range of different kinds of events, and all of them matter equally. On one side: scrappy, rep-led grassroots events alongside our Territory Managers - think farm BBQs, pub shouts, small on-farm gatherings, where the whole point is trust, not polish. On the other: our biggest national and high-profile events, where Halter needs to show up with genuine power and stand out from everyone else in the room. You'll support both, and everything in between, learning when an event needs to be unpolished and authentic, and when it needs to be premium and unmissable.

This role involves regular travel around the country for events, and requires a full driver's licence.




WHAT THE ROLE LOOKS LIKE:

 - Supporting grassroots, rep-led events at scale working closely with our sales team, you'll help support the team running frequent events that build trust on the ground - farm BBQs, open days, welcome events. You'll make sure every one is tracked, lead-gen is captured, and TMs feel genuinely supported rather than left to organise it themselves.

 - Supporting national and high-profile events.  You'll play a hands-on role in our biggest brand moments - the events built to make Halter stand out at scale. This means logistics, supplier coordination, on-the-ground execution, and making sure every detail holds up to the standard these events demand.

 - Execution and logistics.  You'll own the details that make events run smoothly: venue bookings, supplier coordination, travel and accommodation, merch and signage. On event days, you'll be on the ground handling setup, registrations, and troubleshooting whatever comes up. You'll also run pre- and post-event comms including invitations, reminders, follow-ups, surveys, working with the content team to make sure everything's clear, accurate, and on-brand.

 - Working cross-functionally.  You'll work closely with Territory Managers, sales, and the wider marketing team to keep everyone aligned and prepared. That means making sure sales understands the purpose of each event, marketing has what they need to support you, and information flows clearly so nothing falls through the cracks.

 - Tracking results.  You'll help track event outcomes: registrations, attendance, pipeline impact, and pull together feedback and learnings to make the next event better than the last.
   


WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR:




 - Ready to roll up your sleeves.  You enjoy getting into the details and making things happen. Organised, reliable, and you take ownership of your work without needing to be chased.

 - A clear and confident communicator. You're comfortable talking to anyone. Territory Managers, suppliers, farmers at a BBQ, or a stakeholder at a national event. Friendly, practical, and you ask questions when something's unclear rather than guessing.

 - Keen to learn and grow.  You're building a career, and you want the range: grassroots and high-production. You take feedback well and are motivated to keep getting better. There's a real path here to grow into a more senior role as you build that range.

 - Calm and capable.  You stay level-headed when plans change or something goes wrong on the day. You're solutions-oriented, know when to escalate, and help the team keep moving.




OUR BENEFITS 




 - Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

 - Travel: With producers spread across Australia, you’ll be on the road regularly. Expect 3 to 4 days a week and some nights away from home.

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard. 

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund https://foundersfund.com, Bessemer Venture Partners https://www.bvp.com/, BOND, https://www.bondcap.com/ DCVC https://www.dcvc.com/, Blackbird https://www.blackbird.vc/, Promus Ventures https://www.promusventures.com/, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures https://www.icehouseventures.co.nz/?utm_term=icehouse%20ventures&utm_campaign=Brand+Keywords&utm_source=adwords&utm_medium=ppc&hsa_acc=4064636360&hsa_cam=16902737884&hsa_grp=134004309485&hsa_ad=592971340272&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-1082530126230&hsa_kw=icehouse%20ventures&hsa_mt=b&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&gclid=Cj0KCQjw2v-gBhC1ARIsAOQdKY0J0DepRVFDmjQlAkJPbZuQnLSA5UVzUzOXYiPxkjX-SeVa513_BhkaAr-MEALw_wcB.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.

The Role

Halter builds hardware that works in some of the most demanding environments on earth. The quality of what we ship matters enormously, to the farmers who depend on it every day and to the mission we're on. As we scale into multiple products and higher volumes, we need someone to own quality across the full supply chain and build it into a genuine competitive advantage.

The Director of Supply Chain Quality owns Halter's end-to-end quality function, based at our Auckland HQ. You'll lead two teams: a Supplier Quality team that owns quality at our component suppliers from pre-selection auditing through to ongoing part approval, and a Contract Manufacturing Quality team that owns incoming, in-process, and outgoing quality at our contract manufacturers. Together they form a quality system with clear accountability and no gaps.

A critical part of this role is owning Halter's quality assurance specifications, developed and maintained in collaboration with the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team. These specs are the backbone of the quality system. Getting them right and keeping them current is what makes everything else work.

You'll set the quality strategy, develop your team leaders and their teams, own the quality framework across the supply chain, and be the escalation point when quality issues arise at the boundary between supplier and CM. You'll work closely with hardware engineering, operations, and sourcing to ensure quality is designed in and not just inspected for.

This is not a documentation role. The best quality leaders get into the detail. They visit suppliers, they walk the production line, they dig into the data behind a failure mode, and they develop a sharp instinct for what actually drives quality outcomes versus what just adds paperwork. We want someone who is technically curious, comfortable getting their hands dirty, and able to distinguish between a process that genuinely improves quality and one that exists to say it exists.

You'll be measured on product quality, supplier and CM quality performance, and your ability to build a quality function that scales with Halter's growth.


What You'll Do

Leadership and Team Development

 - Lead and develop the Supplier Quality and Contract Manufacturing Quality teams, setting clear direction, holding a high bar, and developing strong people in both functions.

 - Build the culture of the quality function: rigorous, fast-moving, low bureaucracy, and deeply connected to the engineering and operations teams.

 - Set clear accountability between the two teams and own the interface between them, ensuring the handoff between supplier OQC and CM IQC is well-governed and issues at the boundary are resolved quickly.

Quality Assurance Specifications

 - Own the development and ongoing maintenance of Halter's quality assurance specifications, working across the Supplier Quality team, the Contract Manufacturing Quality team, and the hardware design team to ensure specs reflect current design intent and are correctly implemented across the supply chain.

 - Ensure QA specs are the single source of truth for what quality standards are required at suppliers and at our CMs, and that they are kept current as products evolve.

 - Define the governance model for how QA specs are reviewed, approved, and updated, and ensure all three teams are aligned on the process.

Quality Strategy and Systems

 - Own Halter's quality management system across the supply chain, ensuring it is fit for purpose, consistently applied, and evolves as the business scales.

 - Build the quality metrics and reporting that give leadership a clear and honest picture of quality performance across suppliers and contract manufacturers.

 - Lead root cause analysis and corrective action on significant quality escapes, ensuring lessons are captured and systemic issues are fixed rather than managed.

 - Collaborate with the Operations Delivery Lead and Head of Supply Chain Strategy to ensure quality risks are visible early in NPI programmes and sustaining activities.


What You Bring

 - Significant experience leading quality functions in a hardware or electronics manufacturing environme
