At Halter, we know how much farmers care - for their animals and their pasture. But the tools they rely on haven’t kept up, and we’re on a mission to change that. Halter helps farmers make smarter decisions - fast. We reckon good pasture management is the key to more productive and sustainable farms. More grass. Healthier soil. Happier animals. And more time back for the people doing the work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for Lead Engineers who perform at the top of the craft. You'll take on the hardest problems, make the calls that matter on the gnarliest design questions, and ship work that the rest of the team learns from. Engineers around you get better because they're working alongside you. We don't mind whether your strengths sit on the frontend, backend, full stack, or on the platform side that gives every other engineer leverage. What matters is that you ship robust, thoughtful work at a level few others can match, and use AI tools well.




THE KIND OF PROBLEMS OUR TEAMS SOLVE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our engineering teams own different slices of that system, but the problems all rhyme:

 - Turning thousands of collars and billions of sensor events into a single, calm decision in a farmer's hand.

 - Modelling the physical world (animals, pasture, terrain) accurately enough to act on in real time.

 - Building mobile and web experiences that hold up at 5am whilst out in a paddock in the rain.

 - Designing platforms and pipelines that scale with our incredible pace of growth without the seams showing.

 - Engineering against constrained hardware, flaky rural connectivity, and the messiness of the physical world, and shipping with pace despite it.

Every team here ships software that has to work in a paddock, not just a browser tab.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Take on the hardest problems and ship the work that proves them out.

 - Make the architectural calls that matter, then back them up by writing the code.

 - Set the standard for thoughtful engineering: clean, observable, easy-to-evolve code and systems.

 - Support and mentor other engineers through design conversations, code reviews, and generous context sharing.

 - Help set the pace and quality bar for engineering at Halter.

 - Help evolve our testing strategies, CI/CD workflows, and infrastructure patterns.

 - Own the reliability and performance of your domain, especially when things get tricky. Every team owns its services end-to-end, with an on-call rotation.

 - Get out on farm. Deep domain knowledge matters, and you'll be expected to develop it.
   
    


YOU'LL BE GREAT IF YOU:

 - Have spent years shipping complex systems in production and have the experience (and scars) to show for it.

 - Stay calm under pressure, have a low ego, and can rally a team through tough or complex work.

 - Think like a product engineer: you care about the customer experience, not just clean code.

 - Know how to use AI tools well to lift team output and focus on the harder stuff.

 - Have grown other engineers by working alongside them, not by managing them.

 - Are comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where adaptability beats perfection.

 - Have worked in cloud environments. AWS is a bonus.

 - A degree in software engineering (or equivalent) is nice to have, but not essential.
   
    


DEPENDING ON WHERE YOU SIT ON THE STACK, SOME OF THESE WILL LAND HARDER THAN OTHERS:

 - Frontend / Mobile: strong UX intuition, modern frontend frameworks (React, React Native a bonus), an eye for performance and polish on real devices.
   
   Backend: building and scaling REST APIs, distributed systems, and event-driven services. Comfort with both relational and non-relational databases. Node.js, Kotlin, Go, or systems that integrate with hardware/IoT a bonus.
   
   Full stack: all of the above, end to end, across web, mobile, and the services that power them.
   
   Platform: you love building tooling that makes the whole company move faster, including the AI tooling that's reshaping how engineers work. Strong AWS and Terraform at scale, with experience across CI/CD, observability, and on-call tooling.
   
    


OUR BENEFITS

 - Delicious snacks

ABOUT THE ROLE

ABOUT THE ROLE:

How do you represent a living, literally breathing farm in an app and then let someone control it from their pocket?

With Halter's solar-powered collars and software, farmers can fence and shift cattle, manage their pasture and the environment more effectively and monitor animal health, all from one app in real time. There is no reference for this, no pattern library, no interaction models to borrow from. We are inventing them.

A farm is alive and always moving: animals, pasture, weather, all changing by the minute. Our job is to turn that into something a farmer can read at a glance and act on with total confidence. The stakes are physical and the visual and interaction bar is extremely high, this is a farmer's entire farm in their pocket, it should feel like it. Beautifully crafted and a joy to use, every day, for years.

We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to lead the design of a significant area of the product experience at Halter. You'll take on some of our hardest problems and help set the bar for what Halter's product experience should feel like. 

Design at Halter is high agency and high impact. We help define what we should build and why, we spend real time with farmers, ranchers and graziers in the field, and we shape where Halter goes next.

 - Own the end-to-end design process, from early discovery and product definition through interaction design, prototyping, visual design, and launch.

 - Partner closely with Product and Engineering to define what we build, why we build it, and how it should work, identifying opportunities and advocating for the farmer.

 - Turn complex, ambiguous problem spaces into experiences that feel simple, intuitive, and trustworthy.

 - Work across multiple product surfaces and teams, balancing the needs of an individual experience with the needs of the broader system. 

 - Use customer insights, real time in the field, data, experimentation, and strong product judgement to inform your work. The best insights come from the paddock, not a dashboard, which usually means gumboots.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is one system: hardware, software, and AI, running live on real farms. Our platform is what turns that ambitious engineering into farmer and rancher impact. Every collar on every cow, every grazing break a farmer sets, and every alert a vet acts on depends on infrastructure that's reliable, secure, and easy for our engineers to build on. As Halter grows globally and our systems handle billions of daily events from the paddock, the platform underneath needs to scale with us - without slowing anyone down.

We're looking for a Senior Engineer to join our Platform team and help build, run, and evolve the systems that everything else at Halter sits on. You'll bring deep technical expertise to a small team, play a meaningful role in shaping how a fast-growing engineering organisation thinks about cloud infrastructure, developer experience, security, and AI-assisted engineering, and have the autonomy to own significant pieces of the work end-to-end.

Day-to-day you'll work closely with engineering teams across the business - backend, ML, and data - to make sure the platform accelerates their velocity rather than gating it. Whether it's evolving our internal AI tooling into something the whole org relies on, building golden paths that make the right thing the easy thing, hardening our cloud security posture, or keeping our collar-to-cloud pipeline rock-solid as we scale, you'll own problems end-to-end. If you want your work to multiply the impact of every other engineer at Halter, this is the role.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Help shape how Halter leverages AI tooling to accelerate development. We've already invested in internal AI infrastructure that engineers rely on day-to-day, and you'll help it grow from an engineering-team tool into something the whole org leans on - contributing to the adoption patterns, the guardrail to the force-multiplier use cases.

 - Build out the tooling, guardrails, and golden paths that make it easy for other engineers to ship safely and quickly. The right paved roads multiply every engineer's impact, and you'll shape where ours go next.

 - Contribute to the technical direction for our cloud infrastructure as Halter scales globally, helping make the architecture decisions that balance velocity, cost, reliability, and operational simplicity.

Halter collars aren’t serviced, aren’t repairable and need to last 6-10 years, anywhere across the globe. The only way we know they will is by testing them relentlessly - and that testing happens in our lab.

As a Test Lab Technician, you’ll be the hands that keep our test lab running. You’ll set up and run tests, move collars between test rigs, put hardware through our production and verification jigs, and keep our equipment maintained, commissioned and calibrated. You’ll also build and modify the test equipment our engineers need, and take ownership of how the lab itself is organised - putting systems in place and holding the standard so that anyone can walk in and find what they need.

This is a hands-on, high-volume, detail-driven role. We’re looking for someone who wants to be genuinely excellent at running test lab operations.  - Set up, run and monitor hardware tests to the documented test plans

 - Move, install and reconfigure collars across test setups

 - Put collars through our production and verification test jigs.

 - Own the day-to-day maintenance of lab equipment - routine servicing, calibration checks, consumables, and getting faulty equipment back into service quickly.

 - Move, install and commission new equipment into the lab, working with suppliers and internal teams to get it up and running and safe to use.

 - Assemble and modify test equipment, fixtures and jigs, including support for delivering on the test equipment builds committed for Q3.

 - Implement and maintain the organisation systems the lab needs - labelling, storage, sample and unit tracking, consumable stock levels.

 - Keep clear records of what was tested, when, on what equipment and with what result, so investigations and reports can rely on the traceability.

 - Communicate proactively with the Hardware Test team on test status, blockers, equipment issues and timelines

 - Follow and improve lab safety and housekeeping practices, raising hazards and near-misses as you see them.

 - Other duties as required from time to time.


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Hands-on experience in a lab, workshop, production or field service environment - an electronics, mechatronics or engineering background.

 - Practical hands-on skills: comfortable with hand and power tools, mechanical assembly, basic soldering and wiring, and using test equipment such as multimeters and power supplies.

 - Genuine care for accuracy and process discipline - you follow the test procedure as written, record data properly, and speak up when something doesn’t look right rather than letting it through.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Network team owns the wireless backbone that connects every collar to the Halter platform, moving half-a-billion messages between the backend and collars per day! That touches LoRa-based communication protocols, cellular backhaul, the tower network itself, and the edge-to-cloud pipeline that turns radio traffic into real-time telemetry farmers and ranchers can trust. As Halter scales across new farms, regions, and terrain, this network has to scale with it — reliably, because cows don’t take days off.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Network Engineer to take ownership of the performance, reliability, and scalability of Halter's collar and tower network. You'll operate at the intersection of wireless communication protocols, tower infrastructure, and real-time data flow — diagnosing issues from the field, designing the architecture that prevents them, and setting the technical direction for how the network evolves as Halter grows.

This is a senior, hands-on technical role. You'll be the person other engineers come to with the gnarliest wireless and infrastructure problems, and you'll be expected to make the calls that matter when it counts.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Work across technical and commercial teams to understand on-farm connectivity challenges and translate them into actionable requirements that improve the performance and reliability of Halter's IoT network.

 - Take ownership of the operation and optimisation of Halter's collar and tower network, ensuring robust performance, scalability, and minimal downtime.

 - Design and evolve the network architecture, with a focus on wireless communication protocols (e.g. LoRa), tower infrastructure, edge-to-cloud data flow, and real-time telemetry processing.

 - Drive continuous improvement of network health through monitoring, data analysis, and field feedback — proactively identifying coverage gaps, latency issues, and interference patterns.

 - Lead tower deployment strategy, including site selection, configuration, provisioning automation, and remote management, to enable zero-touch scalability.

 - Help set the technical vision and direction for the network discipline alongside other technical leaders.

 - Partner closely with firmware, backend, and product teams to ensure seamless end-to-end data flow from devices in the field through to the Halter platform.

 - Contribute to cross-functional design discussions, making sure networking considerations — latency, range, throughput, redundancy — are well represented in product decisions.

 - Own the rollout and support of networking tools and diagnostics that help teams debug communication issues and understand device behaviour across varied terrain and conditions.

 - Mentor fellow engineers, sharing best practice in wireless networking, telemetry scaling, and high-availability systems.

 - Implement and improve observability for network performance, using tooling and data pipelines that make system health visible and actionable.

 - Help plan and prioritise work within the Network team, ensuring rapid value delivery and long-term reliability.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a rare opportunity to be one of Halter's first Regional Sales Managers (Oeste Arenoso), Argentina — one of the world's great cattle nations — building our customer presence in the region from the ground up.

We're looking for a go-getter who is out in the field, meeting farmers, championing Halter and converting them into our very first local customers. A 'never give up attitude' is crucial for this role; as our first sales hire on the ground, you will be a foundational contributor to the growth and success of Halter in Argentina.

You'll be responsible for using your strong sales background to drive end-to-end sales, from cold calling and on-farm meetings to deeply understanding our customers' farm systems. You'll detail Halter's value proposition, progress the sale, and ultimately close the deal. As the region scales, you'll help shape how we set quotas and commissions, build sales capability, and mentor the team that follows you.  - Laying the groundwork for the local sales function — helping to set and manage quotas, commissions and other sales management tasks as the team grows.

 - Coaching, mentoring and developing future sales staff to help drive their professional growth and reach targets as we scale the region.

 - Collaborating with Customer Success to ensure successful post-sales handoff, implementations, customer satisfaction and account renewal.

 - Providing support, insight and communication to help build and foster trusting and enduring relationships with customers as they wait for deployment.

 - Leveraging opportunities and participating in relevant industry/Halter events and demonstrations.

 - Building and leveraging industry relationships to establish and maintain Halter's brand in a brand-new market.

 - Focusing on the customer and their needs, providing feedback to help drive the product roadmap.

 - Working with the team to optimise and evolve the sales process to become faster, more efficient and more predictable as the company scales.
   


WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR 

 - A complete end-to-end sales skill set with at least five years of experience.

 - Proven track records and examples of successfully sourcing new prospects, securing meetings with new leads and creating new sales opportunities.

 - Someone highly experienced in value-based sales with a proven history of closing deals and high-volume sales results.

 - Well-prepared with solid communication skills to present Halter's value proposition.

 - Experience in beef farming or within the agricultural sector is highly desirable.

 - A person who is results-driven, highly motivated with exceptional time management skills.

 - Adaptability in a high-stakes sales environment and the ability to think on your feet — comfort with the ambiguity of building in a new market is a big plus.

 - Sales experience in the technology-based industry is preferred.

 - Fluency in Spanish, with professional working English to collaborate across our global team.

 - A university degree or equivalent would be excellent but not a must.

When something is wrong, we need someone on the ground who can get to the root cause fast, push through to a real fix, and prevent it from happening again.

The Supplier Quality Principal is Halter's senior technical authority embedded in Asia. You'll lead highly technical supplier audits, own complex quality problem-solving at our suppliers, and work directly with both suppliers and Halter's design teams to ensure that what comes off a supplier's production line meets the standard we set. You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy, covering a portfolio of suppliers across the region and acting as the technical bridge between our Asia supply base and the Halter team in Auckland.

This is not a compliance role. Ticking audit checkboxes and filing reports is not what this job is about. The best person for this role is someone who goes deep: who can walk a production line and immediately identify what's controlling quality and what isn't, who can sit with a supplier's engineers and work through a failure mode from first principles, and who knows the difference between a corrective action that actually solves a problem and one that just looks good on paper.

You'll report to the Head of Supplier Quality and work closely with Halter's hardware design and operations teams. When there's a quality issue in Asia that needs solving, you're the person we call.

You'll be measured on the technical quality of audits, the speed and effectiveness of issue resolution at suppliers, and your ability to build supplier capability over time.

 - Lead technically rigorous audits of Halter's component suppliers across Asia, going well beyond system compliance to assess process control, measurement capability, and the reliability of how suppliers actually build and inspect parts.

 - Identify the real drivers of quality performance at a supplier, not just the documented procedures, and develop clear, prioritised findings that distinguish between critical risks and cosmetic gaps.

 - Conduct pre-qualification audits of new suppliers, assessing their technical capability and readiness to meet Halter's design and quality requirements before commitments are made.

 - Run periodic surveillance audits to verify that corrective actions have been implemented effectively and that quality performance is being sustained.

 - Develop and continuously improve Halter's audit methodology and supplier assessment criteria, ensuring audits capture what actually matters for component quality.

 - Own the resolution of complex quality issues at suppliers, using first-principles analysis to identify root cause and drive effective corrective actions rather than superficial fixes.

 - When a production failure or OQC rejection occurs, lead rapid on-site analysis with supplier engineers and Halter's design team to understand the failure mode, assess risk to in-flight inventory, and define the fastest path to resolution.

 - Work with suppliers to improve their process controls, measurement systems, and inspection methods so that quality issues are caught and corrected at source, not downstream.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/halter-limited & Instagram https://www.instagram.com/lifeathalter/.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Five hundred cattle stand up and walk calmly to their next grazing area. No fences, no dogs, no quad bikes. People say it looks like magic. It is actually solar-powered collars, satellite and mesh connectivity, and machine learning that knows when a cow has eaten enough, how much pasture is left, whether she is healthy, and even who her friends are. Most of this technology did not exist five years ago. We invented it, and we are not slowing down.

You won’t be billing your life in six-minute increments, polishing other people's ideas. At Halter you sit inside a world-class engineering team that ships novel radio protocols, bespoke electronics, firmware, and machine learning at a rapid pace, and we are filing aggressively to hold our global lead. Your job is to find the inventions, sometimes before the engineers realise they have made one, and lock them in.

You will be the second member of our IP team, which means you get to shape how this is done. You’ll bring the patentability analysis, drafting, and prosecution firepower, and you will build the scalable, AI-enhanced systems a rapidly expanding portfolio needs. Expect to spend real time with engineers, reading design docs and code, asking questions until you actually understand how it works, and turning what you find into claims that hold up.

We are adding 500 roles in the next year. That is a constant firehose of new ideas and products.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE:

 - Partner with engineering teams to identify patentable, commercially valuable inventions and draft specifications and claims across firmware, software, machine learning, electronics and mechanical systems.

 - Manage patent prosecution end to end, including examination responses, amendments and strategy, with support from external counsel.

 - Lead freedom-to-operate clearances, working closely with the engineers building the technology.

 - Develop AI-enhanced tools across the IP function. We already use AI heavily and want someone excited to take this further.

 - Join hackathons, uncover patent whitespace, spend time on-farm—and never fill in a timesheet.




YOU'LL CRUSH THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have circa 5-10 years’ experience as Patent Attorney or Patent Engineer.

 - Bring strong technical expertise, or serious interest, across software, electronics or machine learning. We’ll teach you the cow part.

 - Have a real curiosity about how things work. You will dive into design documents and code to find inventions before they are even written down, and keep asking engineers questions until you actually understand it.

 - Have solid experience in patentability assessments, drafting, and prosecution, plus freedom to operate and invalidity work.

 - Have the itch to automate. You see a manual process and you want to kill it.

 - Are comfortable working self-directed. You figure out what needs doing and do it.




BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE:

 - A background or real interest in agriculture and agricultural technology.

 - A legal background or litigation experience.

 - An appetite to get stuck into anything you think might matter to Halter, whether or not it says IP on it.




OUR BENEFITS:

 - Delicious snacks and drinks are available for your daily flow.

 - Healthy body, healthy mind. We're partnered with Southern Cross Health Insurance to support your well-being.

 - We offer 6 months of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers, 4 weeks of fully paid secondary caregiver leave and many other parental benefits that support you and your family.

 - Our personal growth is important. Halter offers an annual $1000 self-development budget to be used for anything that fuels personal growth.

 - Our time to recharge is valued, we're offered wellness leave and unlimited paid annual leave.

 - Importantly, we offer an inclusive and attractive remuneration package made up of salary, benefits and an employee stock ownership plan.




OUR OFFICE FIRST APPROACH:

Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Halter is a dynamic fast paced workplace where our Guidance team is working on Halter’s market leading virtual fencing technology. We are transforming the agriculture industry globally, and you can be a part of that!



We are looking for a Research & Development Specialist to join the team that is continuously developing our virtual fencing product. Everything you need to know to nail this role you’ll learn on the job and you’ll have to work hard to keep up. In this role you’ll be supported to become an expert in virtual fencing. This role is primarily based in the Waikato on our R&D farm close to Morrinsville, where we’ve built our own office in an old calf barn, but you’ll also spend plenty of time in our HQ in Auckland.



The on-farm Research & Development crew has been around as long as Halter and had a huge impact on Halter’s journey; from developing the original Cowgorithm™ to Halter’s expansion into the beef industry, Australia and the US. And we’re only just getting started, so we are looking for someone who is eager to get stuck in and join this unique team.



What does a Research & Development Specialist do?

As you’ll start to become familiar with the basics of our product, you’ll be supporting and running small projects. We’ll teach you how to use our internal tools to analyse all the data our collars generate and you’ll be testing and validating new versions of our software on our R&D farm.



As your understanding of our product increases you’ll be working closely with our engineers to design and develop new features and functionalities. Most of our R&D starts with some crazy idea that we work out on a whiteboard. You’ll be testing and validating the first prototype and will be supporting the implementation into the product.

Once you know all the intricacies of our system you’ll be independently running trials, visiting Halter farms when they require on-the-ground support and could play a role in our international expansion if you’re up for it.



What we’re looking for

For this role we value hunger over experience! Whether you have loads, little or no experience in Research and Development, we want to hear from you! We’re looking for someone that is incredibly motivated, loves solving hard problems and has an incredible attitude. You can’t be afraid to get your hands dirty though, because about half of your work will be outdoors on our farm. Cattle are amazing and intelligent animals to work with and you should be as least as excited about working with them as we are.

If you love the unknown, are hungry for adventure and have a strong desire to learn new things, then this might be the right role for you. It’s important to you that your work matters and you want to have an impact on people, animals and a global industry.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We're looking for a Product Manager to join our Virtual Fencing team, focused on mapping. Please note this role is based at our Auckland HQ.

Mapping is the foundation of Halter’s virtual fencing. Before we can guide a single cow, we need a digital version of the farm or ranch: every fence line, every gate, every water trough, in the right place. We use that map, and the context of each farm or ranch, to guide more than 1.5 million cows every single day.

This role is all about deeply understanding how our product works and what our farmers need from it, then taking those insights and converting them into solutions. This role sits right at the intersection of technology and farming. You'll become the expert in virtual fencing and own mapping end to end: the tools farmers use, the tool our mapping team uses, the imagery and accuracy underneath it all. As we grow across New Zealand, Australia, the US and South America, we need to scale our mapping solutions so we continue to improve farmers' and ranchers’ lives.

You don’t necessarily need any Product Management experience but it’s crucial you’ve got top notch critical thinking skills. If you’re curious, hungry to learn, love solving hard problems and are passionate about agriculture, let’s talk!

 - You love working at a fast pace with loose requirements. You’re confident navigating uncertainty, breaking down messy problems, testing ideas, pivoting and getting stuck in.

 - You can clearly and simply communicate concepts or decisions to engineers, farmers and other Halter teams.

 - You sweat the details because you know they matter, especially for complex products used in demanding, real-world environments.


WHO DAY COULD LOOK LIKE:

 - You will get out on farm regularly, gumboots on, talking to farmers about their operation, understanding how Halter fits into their day.

 - Spend time with our internal mapping team, understanding how they work and where the tool slows them down.

 - Work out what farmers truly need (not just what they're asking for) and how it should work in a real dairy or beef environment.

 - Help decide what gets built next and why, prioritising based on what'll make the biggest difference on farm and help us scale.

 - Work closely with other Product Managers, Engineers and Designers to get features built and shipped.

ABOUT THE ROLE:




As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative.

This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction in this role, you will prioritise daily efforts that optimise growth performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and other regional sales teams, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of farmers.

Your contributions will directly support Halter’s mission to support 50% of the world's habitable landmass to be more productive and sustainable.

Location - This role is to be based anywhere in North Western Victoria. Frequent travel is required as part of the position.

 


WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR

 - Sales & Customer Success Expertise: Value-based sales experience, with a strong history of creating opportunities, closing deals, and building lasting customer relationships. You understand post-sales value building and have experience upselling to grow partnerships.

 - Beef Industry Experience: You know the ropes of beef operations, understanding the unique challenges of the industry. If you don’t, you will be deeply passionate about it, and willing to dive deep into the operations of a farm to learn rapidly.

 - Attitude: You naturally play for the front of the jersey. Make those around you better. Thrive under pressure and own your results. You bring authentic energy and passion to every interaction.

 - Territory Management: Able to use critical thinking to manage a large territory with a balanced focus on sales and customer success, making the appropriate trade-offs.

 - Problem Solving & Collaboration: Resourceful and quick-thinking, you work well with cross-functional teams to address challenges and drive solutions.

 - Willingness to Travel: Frequent travel within your territory to engage with customers and prospects.

 


WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Prospecting & Expansion: Sourcing new leads and opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals, industry events, and other channels, as well as responding to inbound queries. You’ll manage the full sales pipeline from lead generation through to close.

 - Hitting Sales Targets: Manage your pipeline and meet high-growth sales targets by screening, qualifying, demonstrating the product, and successfully negotiating contracts with customers.

 - Customer Account Management: After the sale, maintain close relationships with customers to ensure their ongoing satisfaction, provide support, and address any challenges they face with Halter’s products. You’ll also ensure a smooth handoff from sales to customer onboarding and deployment of Halter, helping customers get the most value from Halter’s solutions.

 - Territory Ownership: A high level of ownership in your territory working with regional agricultural groups to foster deep relationships across the beef industry.

 - Customer Onboarding: Assist in owning the end-to-end customer experience during onboarding and deployment of Halter’s product, ensuring a smooth transition from sales to implementation.

 - Field Learnings & Feedback: Serve as the primary point of contact for gathering customer feedback in your territory. Work closely with Support, Product, and R&D teams to share insights from the field that can drive product improvements and innovations.

ABOUT THE ROLE.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction.

In this role, you will prioritise daily efforts that optimise growth performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and other regional sales teams, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of farmers. This role is based in the Northland region and will require regular travel.

 - Attitude: You naturally play for the front of the jersey. Make those around you better. Thrive under pressure and own your results. You bring authentic energy and passion to every interaction.

 - Territory Management: Able to use critical thinking to manage a large territory with a balanced focus on sales and customer success, making the appropriate trade-offs.

 - Problem Solving & Collaboration: Resourceful and quick-thinking, you work well with cross-functional teams to address challenges and drive solutions.

 - Willingness to Travel: Frequent travel within your territory to engage with customers and prospects.

No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences, just a herd moving at its own pace. People say it looks like magic. Underneath it is a fleet of tens of 1 million (and growing rapidly) collars, each one a small physical system balancing power, radios, sensors and firmware, all operating on a live animal, in the real world, at scale.

We're looking for a Device Systems Engineer to help guide the development of our devices to extract the absolute best performance for our customers. This is a role for someone who wants to build a genuinely deep understanding of the product in the wild: where power gets spent, where the physical world doesn't match the assumptions in the design, and where there's real headroom to do better. You'll spend your time in the data, but the point isn't the data itself. It's the insight it gives you into a physical system, and the improvements you can drive because of it.

This role sits at the intersection of firmware, hardware, comms and data. You'll need to be equally comfortable wrangling a massive, noisy, real-world dataset and reasoning from first principles about what a sensor or a radio can and can't actually do. And critically, you won't just hand off a finding. You'll see it through: forming the hypothesis, proving it in data, working out what to change, and following it into production.

Our team out-thinks, out-works and out-cares. We're committed to delivering real change in the world. This isn't easy, and honestly, we love that it's hard.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Analyse collar performance at fleet scale: power consumption, battery life, GPS and sensor behaviour, across tens of millions of devices operating in wildly different real-world conditions.

 - Wrangle large, messy, real-world datasets (fleet telemetry, logs, field data) to find the signal in the noise, and know the difference between a genuine effect and a data quality artefact.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a motivated, hands-on Field Ops Specialist to join our team as one of our first hardware technicians on the ground in Australia. What is the hardware? The collars and towers that are what makes us Halter. This is a rare opportunity to be part of something genuinely new.

You’ll be responsible for building an efficient operational system from the ground up, getting out onto farms, and making sure our hardware infrastructure runs without a hitch. One moment you’re diagnosing a technical issue in the field, the next you’re delivering collars to a new producer. You’ll be the go-to person on the ground, the kind of person who takes ownership and gets things done.

You’ll work closely with dedicated teams in Australia, and at Halter’s Auckland HQ. You’ll play a key role in making sure our pioneering producers in the region get an unmatched experience from day one.




WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

 - Infrastructure maintenance: Oversee the upkeep and repair of Halter’s on-farm infrastructure to keep operations running smoothly.

 - Hardware diagnosis: Diagnose issues with our hardware and feed that information back to the right team quickly.

 - Deployment support: Get out onto farms to help deploy Halter. Troubleshoot issues, support installations, and make sure things go well.

 - Field insights: Feed your learnings back clearly to our product and engineering teams, so we’re always building what matters most for Australian cattle producers.

 - On-call: Be part of our global on-call roster to support tower-related incidents and proactively find solutions in a timely manner.

 - Data analysis: Collect, interpret, and analyse data from our hardware to optimise processes and improve operational efficiency. Spot issues before they become problems.

 - Maintenance system: Help build and manage a maintenance system tailored to the Australian market.

 - Collaboration: Work closely across Halter’s teams to stay aligned and drive strong customer outcomes.

 - Travel: With producers spread across Australia, you’ll be on the road regularly. Expect 3 to 4 days a week and some nights away from home.

 - Whatever else it takes: You’ll do what needs doing to make Halter continue to succeed in Australia.




WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR

 - Hands-on experience: Practical experience with tools, electrical work, construction, networking, or equipment fitting is a must.

 - Go-getter attitude: You’re proactive, you take ownership, and you’re not afraid to figure things out on the go.

 - Strong communicator: You can translate what you’re seeing in the field into clear, actionable feedback for a remote product and engineering team.

 - Time management: You manage your own time well and get tasks done on schedule without someone looking over your shoulder.

 - Team player: You work well with people across different locations and time zones.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity: This is early-stage market entry. Things will be imperfect. You’ll thrive on that rather than be frustrated by it.

 - Commitment to excellence: You take pride in delivering the best possible service and making sure Halter’s infrastructure is always at its best.

 - Willingness to travel: You’re up for regular and sometimes spontaneous travel across the region.
   
   


JOIN OUR TEAM

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

ABOUT THE ROLE

At Halter, we’re changing the way the world farms - and with that comes a great deal of responsibility to the producers worldwide who trust us with their animals. Our hardware fleet operates across farms and ranches globally, and as we scale, we need better systems, better tooling, and smarter workflows to support our farmers faster and more reliably. We’re looking for a highly motivated Intermediate Field Operations Engineer to join our Field Operations team. This role is ideal for someone with a computer science or software-oriented background who enjoys solving real-world problems, building internal tools, and improving how teams operate at scale.


This role sits at the intersection of hardware operations, customer impact, and engineering. You will spend part of your time running the day-to-day work, such as monitoring fleet performance, triaging issues, working tickets, and coordinating resolution. The other part of your time will be dedicated to designing and building internal tooling, dashboards, automations, and process improvements that make the Field Operations team more effective and allow us to scale globally. You will collaborate closely with Field Engineers, Product, Deployment, Customer Experience, and Software teams to improve how we detect issues, investigate incidents, drive resolution faster, and more consistently.






WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE

Fleet monitoring and operational support

 - Monitor hardware performance metrics to proactively identify collar and tower issues

 - Investigate and respond to technical support tickets related to collar functionality and tower performance

 - Lead investigations end-to-end, from triage through root cause to resolution, deciding when to escalate to relevant teams

 - Collaborate closely with customer teams to ensure efficient handover and resolution of technical issues

 - Communicate cross-functionally with Deployment, Product, and Engineering teams to align on incidents, root causes, and follow-ups

 - Contribute to and maintain internal documentation and knowledge bases for known collar and tower issues

Tooling, systems, and scaling improvements

 - Identify opportunities to remove manual work and improve internal workflows across Fleet Operations

 - Own and build internal tools that support fleet monitoring, investigation, and incident response for a scalable global operating model

 - Improve internal process flows, including triage pathways, escalation rules, investigation checklists, and automation, to reduce time-to-resolution

 - Create systems that help surface issues earlier, such as improved alerting logic, trend analysis, and automated detection of known failure modes

 - Work with engineering teams to integrate tooling with core systems and improve data quality and visibility

Field exposure (optional, as needed)

 - Visit customer farms to work through hardware issues alongside our field-based team where useful



WHAT YOU WILL BRING

 - Hands-on experience in technical operations, support engineering, or a similar role. A background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mechatronics or similar is useful but not required

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down ambiguous problems and turn them into clear next steps

 - Confidence working with systems and data, including dashboards, tools, workflows, logs, and APIs

 - A track record of building tools or automations that others rely on, designing scalable workflows, and making systems easier to operate

 - Strong technical troubleshooting skills with a practical, hands-on approach

 - Excellent attention to detail and the ability to identify patterns in data and turn them into action

 - Clear and concise communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues to both technical and non-technical audiences

 - Strong time management skills and the ability to prioritise across urgent support needs and longer-term improvement work

 - Comfort operating in fast-paced environments where priorities can shift quickly

 - A passion for supporting farmers and ranchers, and contributing to Halter’s mission to change the way the world farms




DEPENDING ON WHERE

A ‘never give up attitude’ is crucial for this role; you will be a significant contributor to the growth and success of Halter in Victoria.

You’ll be responsible for setting and managing quotas and commissions for the Victoria, sales capability management and mentoring for Territory Managers.

You’ll use your strong sales background to drive end-to-end sales, from cold calling and on-farm meetings to deeply understanding our customers’ farm systems. You'll detail Halter’s value proposition, progress the sale, and ultimately close the deal. Make your mark with Halter and help us push the boundaries of farming, connecting animals and humans like never before.

 - Setting and managing quotas, commissions and other sales management tasks for the sales team

 - Coaching, mentoring and developing our junior sales staff to help drive their professional growth to reach targets

 - Sourcing new leads and opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals/introductions, industry events and other channels, as well as fielding and responding to inbound inquiries

 - Meet high growth sales targets by managing pipeline through to close, including screening, qualifying, executing on-farm demonstrations and successfully negotiating contracts with customers

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're building a regional finance and operations hub in Buenos Aires, and this role owns the finance engine for Argentina and Uruguay. Reporting to the Director Finance & Operations, South America, you'll be accountable for the close, tax, statutory compliance and controls across both entities, and you'll lead a Financial Accountant and a Billing Admin from day one.

This is a build role in the literal sense. Some processes exist when you arrive; most don't. You'll design them, run them, and make them hold as volume grows fast. You'll work closely with the Director on planning and strategy, and with Halter's global finance team in New Zealand on consolidation, reporting and group requirements.

If you want to be the person who knows exactly why every number in two countries is right, and who built the process that makes it so, this is it.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The monthly close for Argentina and Uruguay: accurate, on time, and reconciled to group reporting.

 - Tax compliance across both countries (ARCA, formerly AFIP, and provincial Ingresos Brutos in Argentina; DGI and BPS in Uruguay), with advisors managed rather than relied on.

 - Statutory reporting and audits, including inflation-adjusted local reporting and the bridge to group IFRS.

 - Controls and source-of-truth discipline: coding, approvals, documentation and audit-readiness across both entities.

 - Treasury operations: cash positions, FX execution within the policy the Director sets, and import and supplier payment compliance.

 - Leading and developing the Financial Accountant and Billing Admin, and deciding what gets automated rather than resourced.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Must-haves

 - 6 to 10 years in accounting, controllership or audit, with hands-on Argentine tax and statutory experience.

 - You've owned a close end-to-end, not just contributed to one.

 - Working knowledge of inflation-adjusted reporting and IFRS, and the ability to reconcile the two.

 - Fluency in Spanish and English. You'll work daily with the team in New Zealand.

 - Experience managing or mentoring others.

 - Accuracy and a builder's instinct. You're comfortable creating process where none exists.

Nice-to-haves

 - Uruguayan tax and compliance exposure.

 - Big 4 background, or experience in a multinational subsidiary reporting to an offshore parent.

 - Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP.

 - A track record of automating finance processes or using AI to create leverage.




HOW WE'LL KNOW YOU'RE WINNING

 - Close runs on time every month and reconciles to group without back-and-forth.

 - Tax filings and statutory audits in both countries are clean and on time, with no surprises.

 - The Director spends their time on strategy, partnering and operations, not reviewing your work.

 - Your team is growing and taking on more each quarter.




CULTURE LINE

This role is Absolute Ownership of the numbers across two countries: if it's wrong, it's yours to find and fix. It rewards someone who works From First Principles to build processes that scale rather than copying familiar ones, and who brings the discipline of Here to Win to a close that doesn't slip.

Humans are wired for connection. Being office first is a core pillar of our culture because in-person connections drive your growth, learning, impact, and relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful work together.

THE ROLE

Halter is a phase of incredible expansion with hardware right at our core. There are immense challenges and huge opportunities ahead as we grow into new geographies and work towards becoming the operating system for the next generation of agriculture. Our hardware needs to withstand everything from extreme temperatures to cows fighting each other all while continuing to function seamlessly. This requires a technical team with world-class talent, which is where you come in.

Delivery is a new function dedicated to helping engineers and technical teams across Halter do their best work. As the company scales, there is a growing need to keep all the teams working in lock-step with each other. One of the most critical jobs at Halter is to make sure that priorities are aligned and vague, nebulous problems get turned into firm, actionable plans. That’s where you come in.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

You will be responsible for making sure the right people are in the room as you discuss project roadmaps and how to keep things on track. You will see around corners and highlight risks that other teammates did not think of. You will make sure that overhead and unnecessary processes are stripped away so that technical teams have the time and space to execute. You will make sure that all projects are moving at maximum velocity coupled with driving clarity on the path forward across all hardware and operations teams.

Your success will be measured by delivery of projects into mass production. This includes how well you navigated the team through obstacles and the speed at which those problems are resolved.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Coordinate delivering projects across current and future hardware programs. This involves working across hardware design, firmware, reliability, production, operations, and supply chain teams.

 - Build and maintain strong relationships across every discipline. Understand each team's constraints and dependencies well enough to anticipate problems and bring the right people together before things slow down.

 - Lead programs with a lightweight delivery cadence. Make sure that technical teams are not bogged down with process but are aware of what everyone’s responsibilities are and how to move the project forward.

 - Drive clarity and ensure people across the organization and levels are crystal clear about the state of projects and next steps. Be an expert at distilling confusing threads into clear summaries and next steps.

 - Surface trade-offs early and cleanly so decision-makers can move fast.

 - Ensure that engineering builds happen on-time and remove blockers during build execution.

 - Experience driving complex hardware products from development through to production across cross-functional teams

 - Hardware engineering experience. Engineering degree preferred but not required.

 - A mindset for urgency. Everything we work on in the hardware space directly impacts farmers and the company, so velocity is the name of the game.

 - A knack for clear communication. You bias towards zero-inbox and make sure no details get missed without filling slack channels with unnecessary information.

 - Willingness to travel to Asia. A lot of our job requires being hands-on at the factory and supplier sites, and you should have experience in factory environments and influencing suppliers to achieve fast results.

 - Openness to wearing multiple hats. As a scale-up, Halter is still young in its journey to build out the hardware organization. You are not afraid to do what it takes to get projects across the line, even if it does not fall explicitly within your job description.

 - Low ego and comfortable with discomfort. You lean into hard conversations, raise the awkward thing early, and never shy away from tension when it needs to be resolved. You have strong opinions and a desire to solve all kinds of problems, but you hold those opinions loosely and change your mind fast when someone has a better answer.

 - You're fun and a joy to work with. Hardware delivery is intense. You bring energy, humour, and optimism, and people are better for having you around.

New Zealand is our grassroots, home market at Halter, and a pretty unique one at that. You'll be our Revenue Operations presence for NZ, embedded with our Sales team and based in our Auckland HQ. You'll sit within Revenue Operations & Enablement (part of GTM Operations).

This isn't a reporting role or a process maintenance role. You're here to drive performance. Hold the NZ GTM motion to its plan, diagnose what's breaking before it compounds, and build the operational rigour that lets our teams outperform. You'll own pipeline integrity across the NZ funnel, drive conversion and velocity, run the deal desk motion locally, and land the enablement that makes new process actually stick with a field sales team. Post-sale operations, launch and support globally, sit with our Customer Rev Ops Manager, so your focus is the sales cycle.

 - Building reporting that tells leadership what's happening before they have to ask

 - Landing a global process change in NZ, or documenting one you've built here so AU and US can pick it up without starting from scratch

 - Flagging a pattern in NZ handovers or support escalations to the Customer Rev Ops Manager so they can act on it globally

To provide farmers with the highest quality insights, we’re building upon the bleeding edge of scientific advancements with unmatched access to rich, novel data to develop a cutting edge agricultural modelling system. 

You’ll play a pivotal role in one of the machine learning teams within the group, where you could be building advanced models of pasture growth and land properties that power intelligent, modelling animal state, health and activity, and much more. Applications could range from remote sensing of pasture biomass, identification of animal heat events, to grazing interval simulation for advanced recommendations. 

You will be owning end to end development of machine learning pipelines, advanced contemporary modelling, to deployment and monitoring.  - 🛠️Model development: design, dataset construction, training and optimization: Rarely do we utilize a model off the shelf. You will own the architectural design, and all phases of model development.

 - 👀Supporting your work in production: Halter engineers demonstrate a high level of ownership. We support what we build, and we learn from our systems behavior in the field.

ABOUT THE ROLE.

We’re looking for an electronics engineer to take full ownership of key parts of our collar hardware. This isn’t a support role, you’ll be driving design decisions, solving complex problems in the field, and seeing your work through from concept to mass deployment.You’ll work across everything from ultra-low power design, RF optimisation, antenna tuning, and solar conversion, to battery systems, audio, and high-voltage pulse circuits. 

It’s deeply technical and fast-moving, the kind of environment where strong engineers thrive. We want someone who’s excited to build for the real world, not just the lab. Someone who gets energy from turning tough constraints into smart solutions.

 


WHAT YOUR DAY COULD LOOK LIKE.

 - Rapidly design, develop, and test highly reliable electronics for world-leading animal wearables and infrastructure.

 - End-to-end electronic design ownership including component selection, analysis, simulation, schematic design, PCB layout, prototyping, debugging, documentation, manufacturing, and testing.

 - Consistently innovate to improve reliability and hardware performance while minimizing cost to hit ambitious targets.

 - Collaborate with firmware, advanced systems, mechanical, production and farm teams.

 - Design for manufacturing, design for testing, and design for EMC.

 - Develop and execute validation plans to verify all critical features.

 - Root cause analysis of manufacturing and field returns, providing clinical feedback for design improvements.

 


WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR.

Our ideal candidate has:

 - A tertiary degree in Electronics Engineering, or similar relevant qualification.

 - At least 1+ years' professional experience, having grown your craft at a larger engineering organisation before taking on more autonomy.

 - Proven experience designing reliable electronics hardware and successfully delivering those designs into high-volume mass production, ideally including full product lifecycle ownership.

 - Experience designing and implementing circuit boards using MCUs, SoCs, IMUs, GPS, WiFi, LoRa, I2C, SPI, OpAmps, ADCs/DACs, SMPS, LDO and analog/digital mixed-signal design.

 - Experience in ultra-low power IoT electronics design - power generation (solar, high voltage generation and insulation), power conversion (DC-DC), and power consumption/usage optimisation.

 - Proficiency with EE tools (SPICE simulation, oscilloscopes, network analyzers, signal generators, LCR meters, current clamps, HV meters, etc.).

 - Strong organisation, time management, and communication skills.

 - Ability to thrive in a self-driven and demanding startup atmosphere.

 - Based in Auckland, with travel as required to China and Thailand predominantly

 - Previous experience in a startup or scale-up environment is highly desirable but not essential.


OUR OFFICE FIRST APPROACH.

There’s a reason you visit your friends in person, live with your family and don’t do dinners over Zoom. Humans are wired for connection. We believe a world-class, in-person office culture is the best way for high-performing teams.

Being office first is a core pillar of our culture. We believe in-person connections are key to driving your own growth, learning, impact, and building genuine long-lasting relationships. Strong relationships make it easier to disagree, give feedback, and do meaningful and aligned work. We don’t like having heaps of rules or policies, but this means having strong, trusted relationships is critical.

We’re office first, not office only. This means working from the office everyday is our default setting, but we flex when we need to. We have a high-trust culture, so everyone is trusted to do what’s best for Halter.

Our office vibe is something special, it’s hard to describe until you’re here, but people at Halter who have come from fully remote or hybrid companies say they could never go back - the high energy and spectacular people they are now surrounded by everyday makes work so enjoyable. Your growth, your learning and your impact is truly unlimited here, and a big part of that comes from being together solving problems, innovating, building context, and constantly learning from each other.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Work closely with senior engineers to design, build, and maintain backend systems that power our platform.

 - Contribute to feature development, bug fixes, and performance improvements.

 - Participate in code reviews, testing, and documentation to ensure quality and maintainability.

 - Collaborate with product and design teams to bring ideas from concept to production.

 - Learn new tools and technologies, and grow into greater ownership over time.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Typically, 0–2 years of professional experience as a software engineer (internships or projects count!).

 - Solid programming fundamentals and familiarity with at least one backend language (Go, Python, Node, etc.).

 - Curiosity and a desire to understand how complex systems fit together.

 - Eagerness to learn from others and contribute to a collaborative, high-performing team.

 - Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

 - Interest in startups, AI, or logistics a plus.


WHY JOIN CANALS

We're building software that solves real problems for an industry that keeps the world running. Our customers rely on our platform every day to operate their businesses.

postings.title: IT Operations Analyst
postings.descriptionText:
WHO ARE WE?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

 

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

 

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.



Where does this role fit in?

 - Build, operate and continually improve the technology platform that lets every UpGuardian work securely, efficiently and with minimal friction.

 - You’ll own the lifecycle of our corporate technology end to end: identity, endpoints, SaaS and the service practices that hold them together. You’ll automate the repetitive parts, instrument the rest, and make security a property of how systems are built rather than a task someone remembers to do.

 - This is an engineering role, not a ticket queue. If you see the same request three times and your first thought is “why is a human still doing this?” - you’ll fit.

 - Security is an outcome of excellent operational engineering here, not the primary function of the role.



What will you do?

Platform, identity and fleet

 - Google Workspace, Okta (or equivalent IdP), and MDM (Kandji, Jamf or similar) across a mostly macOS and ChromeOS fleet

 - You’ll own SaaS administration and lifecycle, asset management, endpoint standards and compliance, and the joiner–mover–leaver process end to end

Zero Trust and secure access

 - Operate and continually improve our Cloudflare Zero Trust environment across ZTNA, Secure Web Gateway, DNS filtering, tunnels and identity and device aware access policies

 - You’ll help move us away from traditional network trust, maintain secure access to internal applications and services, troubleshoot access and connectivity issues, and make sure security controls don’t create unnecessary friction for employees

Automation and internal tooling

 - Automation is the default approach, not a stretch goal. If a task happens more than twice, it’s a candidate for code

 - You’ll work with REST APIs, Python, Apps Script, Terraform, n8n and AI assisted workflows to build internal tooling that removes work rather than making it faster to do by hand

Service operations

 - Incident, problem and change management. Service catalogue, knowledge base, service metrics, capacity planning and operational readiness

 - You’ll define these practices where they don’t exist yet and improve the ones that do

Reliability and continuous improvement

 - Zero touch provisioning, endpoint compliance, fleet health, monitoring, reporting, SaaS governance and self service. Making internal platforms boringly reliable is the goal

Security, embedded

 - Deploy and maintain security controls, harden endpoints, support security incidents, reduce operational risk and keep baselines current

 - Security is part of how you’ll operate the platform rather than a separate function you’ll own

What will you bring?

You won’t have all of this. Tell us which parts you’d be learning, and we’ll tell you honestly whether that works

 - Depth across enterprise SaaS and identity - you’ve administered Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, an IdP such as Okta or Entra, and MDM at organisational scale. You’re comfortable with SSO, SAML, SCIM, DNS and certificates

 - Zero Trust, hands on - you’ve worked with ZTNA, Secure Web Gateway or modern network access controls, ideally Cloudflare Zero Trust or a similar platform such as Zscaler, Netskope, Tailscale or Entra Private Access. You understand identity and device aware access and the principles behind replacing traditional network trust

 - You don’t need to be a Zero Trust specialist, but you should be comfortable taking ownership of an existing Cloudflare implementation, troubleshooting it and making it better

 - You genuinely automate - you write code using Python, Apps Script or similar, work confidently with REST APIs, and can point to internal tooling you’ve shipped that removed recurring work permanently

 - Fleet management maturity - you’ve worked with macOS at scale, zero touch provisioning and endpoint compliance baselines

 - Service operations experience - you’ve run incident and change practices, defined metrics and built documentation people actually use

 - Security and infrastructure fundamentals - you’re comfortable with endpoint hardening, identity security, DNS, certificates, secure network access and making sensible risk trade offs

 - Process improvement instinct - you make the system better, not just the outcome of one request
   
   

What will give you an edge?

 - Terraform or other Infrastructure as Code

 - Cloudflare

 - n8n or similar orchestration

 - AI and LLM-assisted workflows

 - Deep macOS expertise

 - Chrome Enterprise

 - Working in a security-first or audited environment (SOC 2, ISO 27001)
   
   

What's in it for you?

 - $1500 USD annual Learning & Development allowance: To support your career development, all team members will be able to expense development opportunities against this allowance

 - Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.

 - Personal Leave Allowance: This includes sick & carer’s leave

WHERE DOES THIS ROLE FIT IN?

You’ll be a key member of UpGuard’s Growth Squad, focused on driving organic growth. Based in South Africa and reporting to the Content Writer Manager, you’ll write high-quality content that answers the real questions our prospects and customers are asking, from in-depth articles to comparison and competitor pages on our website.

How people find answers has changed dramatically with the rise of LLMs and AI search engines, and this role is central to making sure UpGuard shows up with content that’s genuinely helpful and conveys authority and trust. Working closely with the Growth Marketing team, you’ll turn research and briefs into accurate, authoritative content, and keep our existing content fresh and competitive.




WHAT WILL YOU DO?

 - Answer the questions that matter: Write high-quality, genuinely useful content that answers the real questions our prospects and customers are asking, whether they find it through a search engine or an AI assistant.

 - Make complex topics clear: Turn cybersecurity and risk concepts into content that’s accurate, insightful, and a pleasure to read.

 - Keep our content at its best: Refresh and improve existing articles and pages so they stay accurate, current, and genuinely helpful.

 - Help buyers make informed decisions: Write and maintain comparison and competitor pages that are accurate, fair, and persuasive.

 - Own your work from draft to live: Publish and format your content in our CMS, including headings, metadata, internal links, and image alt text.

 - See the impact of your work: Work with the Growth Marketing team to review how your content performs and use those insights to make the next piece even better.

 - Maintain Voice and Tone: Ensure every piece of content adheres strictly to the UpGuard brand Voice and Tone.
   
   


WHAT WILL YOU BRING?

 - 3+ years of professional content writing experience, including writing content optimized for search, ideally within the B2B SaaS or Cybersecurity domain.

 - A portfolio of content you’ve written that answers real audience questions, such as long-form articles, comparison pages, or other search-focused content.

 - A solid understanding of SEO and how it’s evolving with AI search, including search intent, keyword usage, content structure, internal linking, and metadata.

 - Hands-on experience uploading and formatting content via a website CMS.

 - Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical or risk management concepts into clear, engaging and authoritative content.

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with an unwavering commitment to editorial quality, consistency and accuracy.

 - Proven ability to manage multiple pieces of content at once in a fast-paced environment, working from briefs with a high level of independence.

 - Strong collaborative spirit, capable of working effectively with web, growth and creative teams.

 - Fluency in English (verbal and written), our primary working language, with a base of operations in South Africa.
   
   


WHAT WILL GIVE YOU AN EDGE?

 - Experience writing content that drives measurable traffic and leads for a business.

 - A background in cybersecurity, vendor risk, or third-party risk management.

 - Confidence using AI tools in your writing process, including refining and elevating AI-generated drafts into accurate, high-quality, human content.

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer - Buenos Aires, Argentina (Hybrid)
postings.descriptionText:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en


ABOUT THE ROLE

Our Engineering team helps Nu create and scale the technology that powers the best financial products in Latin America. We strive for state-of-the-art software development practices, using a variety of technologies and architectures to build resilient, secure, and highly scalable systems.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping the technical direction of multiple teams, driving the design and evolution of large-scale distributed systems that serve millions of customers. While we value experience with our tech stack, we are confident that engineers who are eager to learn will be successful here — and we will teach you Clojure as our main backend language.

 - You will build and evolve
   
   - Horizontally scalable microservices written mostly in Clojure, using Finagle and leveraging functional programming techniques and hexagonal architecture
   
   - High-throughput jobs and inter-service communication using Kafka
   
   - Continuous Integration and Deployment pipelines on AWS
   
   - Data storage solutions using Datomic and DynamoDB
   
   - Monitoring and observability with Prometheus
   
   - Services running as much as possible in Kubernetes
   
   We are a process-light organization that values human interactions. We work in small, independent teams that feel like startups within the company and avoid unnecessary coupling and centralization whenever realistic. We understand that execution is key to success and continuously optimize our processes to remove bottlenecks.

 


YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Setting technical direction for multiple teams, ensuring alignment with Business Areas and architecture strategies

 - Working with large-scale distributed systems and understanding their broad architecture and trade-offs

 - Driving pragmatic innovation while ensuring resilient, secure, and flexible solutions that scale across products and geographies

 - Mentoring engineers across teams and helping maintain a high technical bar organization-wide

 - Writing, testing, instrumenting, documenting, and maintaining high-quality code

 - Pairing and participating in code reviews to support the growth of others in and around your teams

 - Collaborating closely with Product, Design, and Engineering leaders to build new end-to-end experiences

 - Ensuring comprehensive observability, performance monitoring, and robust error handling across team services

 - Participating in on-call rotations for your team and responding to incidents as necessary

 - Focusing primarily on backend applications, while being open to contributing to mobile and frontend development according to business needs


WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PERSON WHO HAS

 - At least 4 years of experience developing digital products in complex environments

 - Deep expertise in distributed systems, microservices architecture, and cloud technologies

 - A proven track record of designing and delivering large-scale systems that serve thousands or millions of users

 - A strong background in object-oriented or functional programming languages, with the ability to work across multiple languages

 - Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives across multiple teams, even without direct authority

 - Experience mentoring senior engineers and raising the technical bar across organizations

 - Practical knowledge of agile software development methodologies and prior experience with CI/CD

 - Strong communication skills to identify and prevent risks, and explain trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - Advanced English skills

 


LOCATION

Buenos Aires, Argentina 
Argentina · Avenida del Libertador General San Martín 1000 – Vicente López

 


OUR BENEFITS

Our benefits are designed to support your wellbeing, development, and life outside of work. They include:

 - Chance of earning equity

 - Health Insurance

 - Life Insurance

 - NuCare

 - International business travel insurance

 - NuLanguage

 - Vacations

 - Parental leaves

 - Work from home allowance

Even if you feel you don't meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply — your unique skills and experiences may be just what we're looking for, and we're excited to learn more about what you can bring to our team.

 


WORK MODEL FOR THIS ROLE

Hybrid 2–3 times/week: Our hybrid work model brings us to the office at least twice a week, on strategic days designed to maximize team connection and collaboration. For more details, visit  https://building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/ https://building.nubank.com/nu-hybrid-work-model/.

Our recruitment process may involve the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools, such as automated interview transcription and analysis, to support the evaluation process. Artificial intelligence is not used to make final hiring decisions; all decisions are made by human reviewers.

To maintain a consistent and fair process for every candidate, Nu does not provide individualized technical feedback. See how our policy works here https://script.google.com/a/macros/nubank.com.br/s/AKfycbwvrewE58oGSbRWIVv8CyCWN68GLxpPVsfYYXv-ZHg94QFsTJmi82rF1x0yt-OTs2W0DQ/exec
